bio.en: Kunal Shah is the founder and CEO of CRED, the Indian fintech app for credit-card bill payments, and a widely followed thinker on why products succeed in India.
bio.zh: 库纳尔·沙阿（Kunal Shah）是 CRED 的创始人兼 CEO，CRED 是一款印度信用卡还款金融科技应用，他也是关于"产品为何能在印度成功"的广受关注的思考者。

summary.en: Kunal observes that many top global CEOs were India-born immigrants who faithfully scaled their founders' "dharma," or core principles. He argues Indian users relate to time and money differently - for instance, no Indian has been paid by the hour. The episode is a fascinating lens on building products for the Indian market and its distinct cultural logic.
summary.zh: 库纳尔观察到，许多全球顶级 CEO 都是印度裔移民，他们忠实地放大了创始人的"达摩"（dharma，即核心原则）。他认为印度用户对待时间与金钱的方式不同——例如，没有印度人按小时计薪。本期提供了一个迷人的视角，来看待如何为印度市场打造产品及其独特的文化逻辑。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Microsoft, Adobe, Alphabet, IBM, Palo Alto Networks, even Starbucks, the CEOs of these companies were all born in India and immigrated to the US.
turns.zh: 微软、Adobe、Alphabet、IBM、Palo Alto Networks，甚至连星巴克，这些公司的 CEO 都出生在印度并移民到了美国。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: A lot of CEOs have done well because they follow the “dharma” of the founders quite well.
turns.zh: 许多 CEO 之所以做得很好，是因为他们很好地遵循了创始人的“法”（dharma）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: “These are the principles that were given to me and I'm going to sustain this and make it even bigger.”
turns.zh: “这些原则是被交付给我的，而我就是要延续它，并把它做得更大。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I want to keep talking about India and how it's different and how to build products that are successful in India.
turns.zh: 我想继续聊聊印度，聊聊它有何不同，以及如何打造在印度取得成功的产品。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: No Indian has ever been paid an hourly salary in their entire life.
turns.zh: 没有一个印度人一生中拿过小时工资。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The concept of time is not the same.
turns.zh: 对时间的概念是不一样的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What do you see as the biggest opportunity for Indian startups?
turns.zh: 你认为印度创业公司最大的机会是什么？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: India is changing because now, for the first time, we are seeing founders being respected and unicorns being celebrated.
turns.zh: 印度正在发生变化，因为现在我们第一次看到创业者受到尊重、独角兽企业受到追捧。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We have a National Startup Day, and probably the first generation that will have to prove ourselves to be very large profitable companies.
turns.zh: 我们有了“国家创业日”，而且很可能是第一代需要证明自己能成为非常大型的盈利公司的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I wouldn't want to be anywhere else building.
turns.zh: 我不愿在别的地方创业。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Today my guest is Kunal Shah.
turns.zh: 今天的嘉宾是 Kunal Shah。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Kunal is one of the most well-known and respected entrepreneurs and product leaders in India and around the world.
turns.zh: Kunal 是印度乃至全球最知名、最受尊敬的企业家和产品领导者之一。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: He shares endless wisdom on Twitter and LinkedIn where he has over 1 million followers.
turns.zh: 他在 Twitter 和 LinkedIn 上分享了无穷的智慧，粉丝超过 100 万。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: He's the CEO and founder of CRED, a FinTech startup based in India, which was last valued at over $6 billion and as of couple years ago processed over 20% of all credit card bill payments in India.
turns.zh: 他是 CRED 的 CEO 兼创始人，这是一家总部位于印度的金融科技初创公司，最近估值超过 60 亿美元，截至几年前，它处理了印度超过 20% 的信用卡账单支付。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Prior to CRED, he founded three other startups including Freecharge, which he sold for over $400 million to Snapdeal.
turns.zh: 在 CRED 之前，他还创办了另外三家初创公司，包括 Freecharge，他以超过 4 亿美元的价格将其出售给了 Snapdeal。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Kunal is a deep thinker, both about product and about life.
turns.zh: Kunal 是一位深思熟虑的思考者，无论是对产品还是对人生都是如此。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: His background is actually in philosophy, which comes across very clearly when you hear him share his advice.
turns.zh: 他其实有哲学背景，当你听到他分享建议时，这一点非常明显。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: In our conversation, we get deep into what makes working and building in India different from the US markets and other markets, including why trust is so essential and why so many people are so much more risk-averse in India.
turns.zh: 在我们的对话中，我们深入探讨了在印度工作和创业与美国市场及其他市场有何不同，包括为什么信任如此重要，以及为什么印度有那么多人更厌恶风险。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We talk about the biggest challenges and opportunities within the India market, why there are so many successful Indian immigrants in CEO roles across tech, and what we can learn from that.
turns.zh: 我们聊到了印度市场内部最大的挑战与机遇、为什么科技行业有那么多成功的印度裔移民担任 CEO，以及我们能从中借鉴什么。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Also, why companies in India can quickly grow DAUs but not ARPUs, and what that means for building products in India.
turns.zh: 还有，为什么印度的公司能快速增长日活用户（DAU）却无法提升每用户平均收入（ARPU），以及这对在印度打造产品意味着什么。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We also talk about how to stay curious and open-minded and the power of second order thinking.
turns.zh: 我们还聊到了如何保持好奇和开放的心态，以及二阶思维的力量。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Also, stories of failure, lots of contrarian takes and so much more.
turns.zh: 还有失败的故事、许多反共识的观点，以及更多内容。

turns.en: If you enjoy this podcast, don't forget to subscribe and follow this podcast on your favorite podcasting app or YouTube.
turns.zh: 如果你喜欢这档播客，别忘了订阅并在你最喜欢的播客应用或 YouTube 上关注本节目。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's the best way to avoid missing future episodes and it helps the podcast tremendously.
turns.zh: 这是避免错过未来节目的绝佳方式，也能极大地帮助本节目。

turns.zh: 非常感谢我的执行制片人 Cyan，是他牵线联系到了 Kunal。

turns.zh: 作为一家企业，你关心营收；但作为产品团队，你最不愿意做的事就是因为团队要从零重建计费系统，而推迟产品发布或定价变更。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Kunal, thank you so much for being here and welcome to the podcast.
turns.zh: Kunal，非常感谢你能来，欢迎来到播客。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Lenny, thank you so much for having me, and a huge fan of everything that you do.
turns.zh: Lenny，非常感谢你邀请我，我可是你所有内容的超级粉丝。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And like I said before, India is a huge beneficiary of what you do.
turns.zh: 就像我之前说的，印度是你所做之事的巨大受益者。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We are all people who have learned the art of product by just figuring it out, and watching some content here and there and reading some stuff.
turns.zh: 我们这些人都是靠自己摸索、这里看看内容、那里读读东西，才学会了产品这门艺术。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So kudos to everything that you do.
turns.zh: 所以为你所做的一切点赞。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And like I said earlier, you do a fabulous job of taking the information asymmetry of the art of product and making it accessible to many of us across the world.
turns.zh: 就像我之前说的，你做了一件了不起的事——把产品这门艺术中的信息不对称，变得让我们全世界许多人都能够理解。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So thank you.
turns.zh: 所以谢谢你。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, I really appreciate that.
turns.zh: 哇，我真的很感激。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is already feeling great to me.
turns.zh: 我已经有非常好的感觉了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I have a huge.. so it turns out this podcast has a huge audience in India, as do you.
turns.zh: 我有个巨大的……事实证明，这档播客在印度拥有庞大的听众，你也一样。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so I feel like this conversation is going to be really special and really meaningful to a lot of people.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这次对话对很多人来说都会非常特别、非常有意义。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I wanted to start with something very tactical.
turns.zh: 我想从一些非常实操的内容开始。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's a product framework that you came up with that I absolutely love, and I've shared it with at least 30 founders over the last couple years. And this is actually how I discovered you initially; I heard about this thing, and I'm like, who's this guy Kunal Shah?
turns.zh: 你提出了一个产品框架，我非常喜欢，过去几年里我已经把它分享给了至少 30 位创始人。其实我最初就是通过这个发现你的——我听说了这个东西，然后就想，这个 Kunal Shah 是何方神圣？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And look at us now, chatting.
turns.zh: 看看我们现在，居然在聊天了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Could you explain this framework briefly and then just how you've used it or how you recommend people apply it?
turns.zh: 你能简要解释一下这个框架，然后讲讲你是如何使用它、或者你建议人们如何应用它吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Oh, and by the way, it's called Delta 4.
turns.zh: 哦，对了，它叫 Delta 4。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I don't know if I even said the name.
turns.zh: 我都不知道我刚才有没有说出它的名字。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Yeah, it's called the Delta 4 framework, but I think it's actually quite simple.
turns.zh: 对，它叫 Delta 4 框架，不过我觉得它其实相当简单。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: If you think about it, a lot of people say that your product has to be 10x better and it's not very measurable.
turns.zh: 仔细想想，很多人说你的产品必须比对手好 10 倍，但这其实很难衡量。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You don't know if you are 10x better or not unless you're delusional.
turns.zh: 除非你自欺欺人，否则你根本不知道自己是不是真的好了 10 倍。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the trigger for me was actually, I'm the unusual tech founder in India.
turns.zh: 而触发我思考这个问题的契机其实是——我是印度一个非典型的科技创业者。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I'm the only humanities/philosophy major founder in India who's got into tech.
turns.zh: 我是印度唯一一个以人文学科/哲学专业背景进入科技领域的创始人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I often wondered if most people who were my peers, or people who were ahead of me, were significantly smarter academically or otherwise.
turns.zh: 我常常在想，那些和我同辈、或者走在我前面的人，是不是在学术上或其他方面明显更聪明。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And why did I become successful with my first startup, Freecharge, which I exited in 2015 for nearly $450 million?
turns.zh: 为什么我的第一个创业项目 Freecharge 能成功，并在 2015 年以近 4.5 亿美元退出？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I was like, “What would make this happen?”
turns.zh: 我当时就在想，“到底是什么让这一切发生的？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Because I would not qualify into this super league of really top IIT rankers that exist in India.
turns.zh: 因为我根本不够格进入印度那些顶尖 IIT（印度理工学院）排名高手的超级联盟。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that got me onto this philosophical quest to find out what makes things successful.
turns.zh: 这让我踏上了一场哲学探索，去寻找究竟是什么让事情成功。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So the simple framework is, an example I give often is that, imagine the old way of taking a cab ride and an Uber. And if I asked you to give me the score of efficiency on Uber and let's say getting the old cab, what would you say, Lenny?
turns.zh: 所以这个简单的框架是——我经常举的一个例子是：想象一下以前打车的方式和 Uber 的区别。如果我让你给 Uber 的效率打分，再给老式出租车打分，你会怎么说，Lenny？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I'm curious.
turns.zh: 我很好奇。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Out of 10?
turns.zh: 满分 10 分？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah, give a cab three and then Uber like a nine.
turns.zh: 对，给出租车 3 分，Uber 大概 9 分。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So every time you see that the product efficiency delta is greater than or equal to four, three things happen.
turns.zh: 所以每当你发现产品的效率差值（delta）大于等于 4，就会发生三件事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It is irreversible.
turns.zh: 第一，它是不可逆的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Second is that you have a very high tolerance for it to fail.
turns.zh: 第二，你对它的失败有很高的容忍度。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: If Uber fails a little bit, will you say, “Oh my God, I'm going to really stop using it?”
turns.zh: 如果 Uber 偶尔出点小问题，你会说“天哪，我真的要弃用它了”吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: No.
turns.zh: 不会。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the third thing is what I call the UBP, ‘Unique Brag-worthy Proposition.’
turns.zh: 第三件事是我所谓的 UBP——“独特的、值得炫耀的卖点”（Unique Brag-worthy Proposition）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Every time humans unlock a Delta 4 product or service, they cannot stop talking or sharing about it.
turns.zh: 每当人们解锁一个 Delta 4 的产品或服务，他们就会停不下来地谈论它、分享它。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore all Delta 4 products will naturally have lower CAC or sometimes zero CAC because people, humans.. and think about it, Lenny, how you discovered Google, definitely not through an ad, definitely not through some performance marketing here and there.
turns.zh: 所以所有 Delta 4 产品天然就会有更低的获客成本（CAC），有时甚至是零获客成本，因为人们……Lenny，你想想，你是怎么发现 Google 的？肯定不是通过广告，肯定也不是通过那些零散的效果营销。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Somebody showed you the demo and you were like, “Oh my God, this is crazy.”
turns.zh: 是有人给你演示了一下，然后你就“天哪，这也太神奇了。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that's what I'm seeing right now, what's happening with everything on OpenAI and everything that is happening around LLM feels like magic and it's Delta 4 because the efficiency of doing things before and after is now showing that.
turns.zh: 而我现在看到的正是这样——围绕 OpenAI 和大型语言模型（LLM）发生的一切都像魔法一样，它就是 Delta 4，因为做同一件事在之前和之后的效率差异现在显现出来了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But failure is the real problem.
turns.zh: 但失败才是真正的问题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And making everything tech does not make things more efficient.
turns.zh: 而且，把一切都技术化，并不意味着事情就会更高效。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Let's take an example.
turns.zh: 举个例子。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Buying a suit for yourself online versus offline, all tech, cool stuff, all the features built in.
turns.zh: 在线 vs 线下给自己买一套西装——全是技术、酷炫的东西、各种内置功能。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What would you say the efficiency of buying a suit online is versus, let's say, buying a suit offline?
turns.zh: 你会说在线买西装的效率，对比线下买西装，怎么样？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I've actually done that and it was a terrible fit. It did not fit at all.
turns.zh: 我其实试过，结果非常不合身，完全穿不了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so it's efficient, but the end result was not, it's probably often not great.
turns.zh: 所以它（过程）是高效的，但最终结果并不好，大概常常都不怎么样。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So it's probably-
turns.zh: 所以它大概——

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Overall efficiency score, what would you give?
turns.zh: 整体效率得分，你会给多少？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Of buying a suit online?
turns.zh: 在线买西装吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Yeah, versus offline.
turns.zh: 对，对比线下。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'd probably give it five and five.
turns.zh: 我大概会给它 5 比 5。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Offline is actually probably a better experience.
turns.zh: 线下其实可能是更好的体验。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I give it a seven.
turns.zh: 我给它 7 分。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: That's crazy because you've broken the principle, this is a tech product, but the efficiency is better offline.
turns.zh: 这很疯狂，因为你打破了这个原则——这是个科技产品，但线下的效率反而更高。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore when the delta is less than four, what you will discover is that it is reversible.
turns.zh: 所以当差值小于 4 时，你会发现它是可逆的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You will not see people bragging about it and you have zero tolerance for it.
turns.zh: 你不会看到人们拿它炫耀，而且你对它零容忍。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So you're never going to buy a suit online. I can tell you that right now.
turns.zh: 所以你永远不会在线买西装。我现在就可以告诉你。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think it's a simple framework.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得这是一个简单的框架。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I believe that if many companies applied.. I know now many VCs in the US use this as part of the training program for analysts.
turns.zh: 我相信如果许多公司应用它……我知道现在美国很多 VC 把它作为分析师培训计划的一部分。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: omebody in Sequoia mentioned this to me that they have this as part of the thing, but in India we are not still applying many of these things.
turns.zh: 红杉（Sequoia）有人跟我提过，他们把它纳入了培训内容，但在印度，我们还没有好好应用这些理念。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think it's a simple framework to at least know. You can apply this to features, you can apply this to products, you can apply that to business.
turns.zh: 我觉得至少知道这个简单框架是有用的。你可以把它用在功能上、用在产品上，也可以用在业务上。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And oftentimes this is a longer concept.
turns.zh: 而且，这往往是一个更宏大的概念。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We can talk about it in many ways because it's derived out of some study around entropy and evolutionary biology, which is the root of how I discovered and thought about Delta 4, that “When does a species get disrupted ” or “what is entropy and why does low entropy require growth of high entropy?”
turns.zh: 我们可以从很多角度来谈，因为它源自对熵和进化生物学的一些研究，这也是我思考并发现 Delta 4 的根源——“一个物种什么时候会被颠覆？”或者“什么是熵？为什么低熵需要高熵的增长？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's a day long podcast on its own.
turns.zh: 这本身就能聊上一整天。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So some other time.
turns.zh: 所以改天再聊吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We'll save that for a future follow-up, just diving in on the psychology of Delta 4. Just to kind of summarize this, because I think it's such a powerful framework and I find it useful to convince founders why their product isn't taking off.
turns.zh: 我们把它留到以后的跟进节目，专门深入探讨 Delta 4 的心理学。先做个总结，因为我觉得这是一个非常有说服力的框架，我发现它可以很有用地让创始人明白，为什么他们的产品没能火起来。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: They may feel like this is better than. The classic example, is a better Excel.
turns.zh: 他们可能觉得“这比（现有方案）好”。经典的例子就是“一个更好的 Excel”。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Look, this is so much better than Excel.
turns.zh: 看，这比 Excel 好太多了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It can do all these things.
turns.zh: 它能做所有这些事情。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You don't have to learn all these formulas.
turns.zh: 你不必学习所有这些公式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: But the trick here that I love is just what people rate the existing solution 1to 10, what would they rate your solution 1 to 10?
turns.zh: 但我最喜欢的一个诀窍是：人们给现有方案的打分是 1 到 10 分中的几分，他们会给你的方案打几分？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It has to be four points higher, otherwise no one's going to pay attention.
turns.zh: 必须高出 4 分，否则没人会关注。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I think it's pretty simple.
turns.zh: 我觉得这很简单。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: People are busy, they have enough things to do, they have enough products and apps, they're not going to take the time to really dig into something if it's not that much better.
turns.zh: 人们很忙，他们要做的事情已经够多了，已有的产品和 App 也够多了，如果一样东西没有好很多，他们是不会花时间去认真研究它的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 完全同意。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm going to go in a totally different direction.
turns.zh: 我要换个完全不同的话题了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I want to talk about Indian CEOs in the US.
turns.zh: 我想聊聊在美国的印度裔 CEO 们。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So today the CEOs of Microsoft, Alphabet, Adobe, which is a $250 billion company it turns out, IBM, which is a $170 billion company, Palo Alto Networks, which is a $100 billion company, even Starbucks, also a $100 billion company, I was looking that up.
turns.zh: 当今，微软、Alphabet、Adobe（我查了一下，这是一家 2500 亿美元的公司）、IBM（1700 亿美元的公司）、Palo Alto Networks（1000 亿美元的公司），甚至连星巴克（也是一家 1000 亿美元的公司），他们的 CEO……我查了这些数据。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And then also Twitter before Elon took over Twitter. The CEOs of these companies were all born in India and immigrated to the US.
turns.zh: 还有埃隆接管之前的 Twitter。这些公司的 CEO 都出生在印度并移民到了美国。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I might be wrong, but I think this is the largest ethnic group of CEOs of tech companies other than just white dudes in the US.
turns.zh: 我可能说得不对，但我认为这是美国科技公司的 CEO 中，仅次于白人男性之外最大的族裔群体。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So I'm curious why you think Indian immigrants are so successful in business and in tech in the US, especially in these very high positions.
turns.zh: 所以我很好奇，你认为为什么印度裔移民在美国的商业和科技领域如此成功，尤其是在这些非常高的位置上？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I'm most curious, just what can we learn from that?
turns.zh: 而我最好奇的是，我们能从中学到什么？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What can we learn from their success?
turns.zh: 我们能从他们的成功中学到什么？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's a great question.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I often wonder about it and I have had the good fortune to meet a fair bunch of these individuals, and had a chance to really explore with them what really went on.
turns.zh: 我常常思考这个问题，也有幸见过其中不少这样的人，并有机会和他们深入探讨到底发生了什么。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So there are a few things that pop out.
turns.zh: 所以有几件事会凸显出来。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And again, these are all conjectures, which I can't prove in any way, but it's a thought experiment to talk about these things.
turns.zh: 再次强调，这些都只是我的推测，我无法从任何角度去证明，但把它当作一个思想实验来讨论这些事是可以的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: First is in general, immigrants that get out of the country usually have a chip on their shoulder in a very different way. And the struggle that they have to go through to just get out and be successful, and that hunger that got them there. There was no privilege.
turns.zh: 首先，一般来说，能走出国门的移民往往带着一种截然不同的“肩上的刺”（证明自己的执念）。他们为了出去并取得成功所经历的挣扎，以及推动他们走到那里的那种饥饿感。那里没有任何特权。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They came from very, very humble backgrounds and literally no money to start with.
turns.zh: 他们出身非常、非常卑微，起初真的身无分文。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think that this force is real.
turns.zh: 所以我认为这种力量是真实存在的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You can say that for many immigrants in general as well. But appreciation for math in general, or logic which came to society in a big way, kind of gave. Let's say for example, lots of engineering graduates come from only a few countries because society was bent towards early exposure to mathematics.
turns.zh: 对许多移民来说你也可以这么说。但总体上对数学或逻辑的重视——它以一种宏大的方式进入社会——某种程度上起了作用。比如，大量工程毕业生只来自少数几个国家，因为那些社会从小就注重数学启蒙。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think that kind of helps create status that will get appreciated.
turns.zh: 而我觉得这在一定程度上有助于创造出会被认可的地位。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, being an engineer, a doctor... As a philosophy major, I was a write-off for society.
turns.zh: 比如，成为工程师、医生……而作为一个哲学专业的人，我在社会眼里是被“放弃”的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So the reason I'm the rare commodity over here, because you are not considered to be very bright unless you break into these very hard exams and do very, very hard things.
turns.zh: 所以为什么我在这里是稀缺品，是因为除非你考过那些极难的考试、做成那些极难的事，否则你不被认为很聪明。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So the filtering criteria on its own is big.
turns.zh: 所以光是筛选标准本身就很严苛。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But there's another interesting framework altogether, which I have actually learned from this gentleman, Devdutt Patnaik. He applies Indian mythology and management principles together.
turns.zh: 但还有另一个完全不同的有趣框架，其实是我从这位先生 Devdutt Patnaik 那里学到的。他把印度神话和管理原则结合在了一起。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And it's an interesting thing. There are three major Indian Gods.
turns.zh: 这很有意思。印度有三大主神。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: One is Brahma, the God of creation, Shiva the God of destruction.
turns.zh: 一位是梵天（Brahma），创造之神；湿婆（Shiva），毁灭之神。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I'm generalizing here, but that's the classification.
turns.zh: 我这里是在概括，但这是基本的分类。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the third is Vishnu, the God of sustenance.
turns.zh: 第三位是毗湿奴（Vishnu），维系之神。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And their avatars-the word “avatar” comes from Vishnu who keeps changing avatars.
turns.zh: 他们的化身（avatar）——“avatar”这个词就来自毗湿奴，他会不断变换化身。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So we have Rama, Krishna, all these Gods are avatars of his.
turns.zh: 所以我们有罗摩（Rama）、克里希纳（Krishna），所有这些神都是他的化身。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So what you notice is that if you take a two by two of people who are high on values and low on values, are high on obedience and low on obedience, you make an interesting two by two.
turns.zh: 所以你会注意到，如果你把“高价值观/低价值观”和“高服从性/低服从性”做一个 2x2 矩阵，你会得到一个有趣的四种组合。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Now, Lord Krishna, who is one of the very popular avatars, which suits the entrepreneurial category, is high on values but very low on obedience. He was known to be the naughty God and he could actually create lots of things.
turns.zh: 现在，克里希纳（Krishna）主是非常受欢迎的化身之一，很适合创业这个类别——他价值观很高，但服从性很低。他以“调皮的神”著称，而且确实能创造出很多东西。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And there is Rama, who is known to be the one who follows principles and is obedient.
turns.zh: 还有罗摩（Rama），他以遵循原则、顺从守纪著称。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So they will follow ‘dharma’ and scale on that.
turns.zh: 所以他们会遵循“法”（dharma）并以此发展壮大。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And then there are these notorious characters, there is Ravana who is low on values, low on obedience, and there is Duryodhana which he says that he is high on obedience but low on values.
turns.zh: 然后还有一些臭名昭著的角色，比如罗波那（Ravana），他价值观低、服从性也低；还有难敌（Duryodhana），按他的说法是服从性高但价值观低。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So these are the people that you don't want to be.
turns.zh: 所以这些是你不想成为的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And what you notice is that a lot of CEOs have done well because they follow the ‘dharma’ of the founders quite well.
turns.zh: 而你会注意到，许多 CEO 做得好，是因为他们很好地遵循了创始人的“法”（dharma）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They have not diluted the dharma of the founders who have started these companies, and managed to sustain that.
turns.zh: 他们没有稀释那些创办公司的创始人的“法”，并设法维系了它。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And a lot of CEOs have this need to say, "Oh, I'm going to change the company forever and it'll be my identity and I will change the logo and I'll change the name and I will do all sorts of things."
turns.zh: 许多 CEO 都有这样一种冲动，想说“噢，我要永远改变这家公司，让它成为我的标签，我要换 logo、改名字、做各种改动。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But maintaining ‘dharma’, where I will say that “These principles were given to me and I'm going to sustain this and make it even bigger," comes from the humility of saying that there is something that was built with some pure form factor, and I think therefore that character stays on.
turns.zh: 但维系“法”，也就是我所说的“这些原则是被交付给我的，而我就是要延续它，并把它做得更大”，源于一种谦逊——承认有某种东西是以某种纯粹的形态建立起来的，因此我认为这种品格得以延续。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore we have the characters of Brahma and Shiva, the founder and destroyer.
turns.zh: 所以我们才有了梵天和湿婆这样的角色——创造者与毁灭者。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: That's the thing.
turns.zh: 就是这样。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But sustenance is the harder one.
turns.zh: 但维系（sustenance）才是更难的那一个。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore our avatars keep happening over time and different hurdles come and then different levels come.
turns.zh: 所以随着时间的推移，我们的化身不断出现，不同的障碍到来，然后不同的境界也到来。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But when you think about the archetype of, at least the Indian CEOs, I've seen that they are fabulous at moving between Krishna and Rama all the time.
turns.zh: 但当你思考——至少印度裔 CEO 的原型时，我发现他们非常擅长一直在克里希纳和罗摩之间切换。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They can play this consistently, and therefore they keep evolving and keep making these companies bigger and bigger.
turns.zh: 他们能始终如一地扮演这两者，因此他们不断进化，让这些公司越做越大。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think we'll see a lot more of this in years to come, because now they have the role models of these individuals who have done well.
turns.zh: 而且我认为未来几年我们会看到更多这样的例子，因为他们现在有了这些做得好的人的榜样。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But the key principle is that if you ask the founders, they will love these CEOs if they're around because they maintain the dharma.
turns.zh: 但关键原则是，如果你去问那些创始人，他们会喜爱这些 CEO（如果他们在世的话），因为这些 CEO 维系了“法”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, what Tim is doing is maintaining the dharma of Steve Jobs because if he had tried to change the dharma of Steve Jobs and the values of the company, it's very hard to imagine it sustaining itself forever.
turns.zh: 比如，Tim（库克）所做的就是维系史蒂夫·乔布斯的“法”，因为如果他当初试图改变乔布斯的“法”和公司的价值观，很难想象它能永远持续下去。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, what an answer.
turns.zh: 哇，这回答太绝了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What I love about this is this combination of using a two by two and Indian mythology. It is like the microcosm of you, which is philosophy and tech.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这一点——它把 2x2 矩阵和印度神话结合在了一起。这就像你的缩影，即哲学与科技的结合。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so I love that and it makes a lot of sense that that's where your mind goes.
turns.zh: 所以我喜欢这一点，而且你的思维会走到那里，是非常说得通的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Something else this makes me think about is, I read this book a long time ago, Jim Collins ‘Good to Great’ or one of his early books about leadership, and he talks about level five leadership I think. Here level five leaders are ones where it's not about them, it's about the business and they can disappear in the future and things will work great.
turns.zh: 这还让我想到另一件事：很久以前我读过吉姆·柯林斯（Jim Collins）的《从优秀到卓越》，或者他早期某本讲领导力的书，我想他谈到了第五级领导力。第五级领导者的特点是，一切不是关于他们自己，而是关于企业，即使未来他们消失了，事情依然运转良好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I feel it is very hard if you believe that your identity needs to have its own position and legacy, and therefore a lot of time chasing status causes disruption because you will say that “Oh, this doesn't have my signature in it.”
turns.zh: 我觉得，如果你认为自己的身份需要有自己的位置和遗产，那就非常难做到，因为很多时候追逐地位会导致破坏——你会说“噢，这里面没有我的印记。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore accepting the religion and trying to be the Pope of it or the father of it is better than trying to say, "Oh, I need to have my variant of religion."
turns.zh: 所以，接受既有的“宗教”并努力成为它的教皇或教父，比试图说“噢，我需要我的某个变体宗教”要好。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that's where the creative destruction starts happening.
turns.zh: 而创造性破坏正是从那里开始的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interesting.
turns.zh: 有意思。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So you said that there's this good balance between Krishna and Rama that happens.
turns.zh: 所以你说，克里希纳和罗摩之间达成了一种很好的平衡。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Can you just summarize where they are in that two by two?
turns.zh: 你能简单总结一下他们在那个 2x2 矩阵里的位置吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Rama is high on values and high on obedience, and Krishna is high on values and low on obedience, but they both are high on values, which means they'll follow dharma, and they'll change sides.
turns.zh: 罗摩是价值观高、服从性高；克里希纳是价值观高、服从性低；但他们俩价值观都高，这意味着他们会遵循“法”，并会在两者之间切换。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, let's say Satya during the OpenAI crisis played Krishna and got things out, but he'll switch back to being Rama and continue to keep scaling it up.
turns.zh: 比如，在 OpenAI 危机期间，萨提亚（Satya）扮演了克里希纳，把事情摆平了，但他会切换回罗摩，继续把它做大。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing.
turns.zh: 太妙了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And just to close the loop on here, is your sense that they're actually thinking about this and they're religious, or is this just in the ether of growing up in India and this is just part of the culture?
turns.zh: 就为了把这个闭环收尾：你认为他们是真的在思考这些、并且信教，还是说这只是成长于印度的氛围中、只是文化的一部分？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's a great question.
turns.zh: 这是个好问题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I don't think they consciously think about it, but I think if they ever heard this, they would agree with it, because that's what they grew up with and value systems are much more long-term.
turns.zh: 我觉得他们不会下意识地去想这些，但我认为如果他们听到这个说法，会表示同意，因为他们就是这样长大的，而且他们的价值体系更偏向长期主义。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, I believe all bad behavior in humans comes from being short-term, and being long-term is a big choice to make.
turns.zh: 比如，我相信人类所有不良行为都源于短视，而选择长期主义是一个重大的决定。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And a lot of times a lot of people argue that we have a 95% arranged marriages and less than 1% divorce rate, comes from this whole long-term thinking that people are married through values versus attraction or lust and all of that stuff. They’re more long-term oriented and about building a family, building values.
turns.zh: 很多时候很多人会说，我们有 95% 的包办婚姻和不到 1% 的离婚率，就来自这种整体的长期思维——人们是基于价值观而非吸引力或欲望等结合在一起的。他们更倾向于长期导向，注重建立家庭、建立价值观。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Or low divorce rate is about “we'll fix along the way” versus trying to say “I need to evolve” and “I need to move forward.”
turns.zh: 或者低离婚率意味着“我们会一路解决问题”，而不是说“我需要进化”“我需要向前走”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think being long-term about that mindset, and that's why some cultures last for thousands of years, because of this need for everybody to be more long-term versus short.
turns.zh: 所以我认为正是这种长期主义的心态，也是为什么有些文化能延续数千年——因为大家都更需要长期而非短视。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: The US could use a lot of that these days.
turns.zh: 如今美国倒是很需要多一点这种心态。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You mentioned this interesting fact about how in India, most startups fail. You said, I think, the classic stat is 90%, and that the risk is a lot higher to start a company and then fail.
turns.zh: 你提到一个有趣的事实：在印度，大多数创业公司都会失败。我想你说过的经典数据是 90%，而且创业失败后风险要高得多。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Can you just talk about what impact that has?
turns.zh: 你能谈谈这带来了什么影响吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: How do people try to avoid that?
turns.zh: 人们如何试图避免这种情况？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Because that'd be amazing if you can reduce the risk of starting a company or is it just that it happens and people get super in debt?
turns.zh: 因为如果能降低创业的风险那就太棒了，还是说这只是会发生、然后人们就背负巨额债务？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think long-term societies are naturally more risk-averse. And not all great CEOs can become great founders for the same reason.
turns.zh: 我认为长期主义社会天然更厌恶风险。正因如此，并非所有优秀的 CEO 都能成为优秀的创始人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: In fact, I would say that it actually makes it very hard to be a founder if you've been a great CEO because you've turned into this sustainer versus destroyer or creator.
turns.zh: 事实上，我想说，如果你是一个优秀的 CEO，反而很难成为创始人，因为你已经变成了维系者，而不是毁灭者或创造者。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The nuance I'm talking about is when you are thinking about risk appetite, India is changing, but now for the first time we are seeing founders being respected and talked about and these unicorns being celebrated and our Prime Minister talks about startups quite openly.
turns.zh: 我想表达的细微差别是，当谈到风险偏好时，印度正在改变，但现在我们是第一次看到创业者受到尊重、被谈论，这些独角兽企业受到追捧，而且我们的总理也相当公开地谈论创业公司。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We have a National Startup Day and so on and so forth.
turns.zh: 我们有了“国家创业日”等等。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think there is a thing that has changed this, but let's understand the core human behavior.
turns.zh: 所以我认为有些东西已经改变了这一点，但让我们先理解人类的核心行为。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: India still has a large number of arranged marriages.
turns.zh: 印度仍然有大量包办婚姻。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you are a founder and a failed founder, your chances of getting a person to marry is still hard to achieve.
turns.zh: 而如果你是一个创始人、而且是失败的创始人，你找到人结婚的机会依然很难。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So if this is all true, then the appetite to take risk will be curtailed.
turns.zh: 所以如果这一切都成立，那么承担风险的意愿就会被削弱。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Somebody gave me an interesting example that there's a very large, let's say CPG company in India, and let's say you do a zero to one over there and the CEO changes in four or five years and your zero to one fails, but you were the best person, that's why you were given the zero to one.
turns.zh: 有人给我举了一个有趣的例子：假设印度有一家非常大的快消品（CPG）公司，你负责从 0 到 1 的项目，四五年后 CEO 换了，你的从 0 到 1 失败了——但你原本是最优秀的人，所以才把这个从 0 到 1 交给你。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The next CEO is like, “So what have you done in the last five years?”
turns.zh: 下一任 CEO 会说：“那你这五年都干了什么？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: He's like, "Nothing.
turns.zh: 他会说：“什么也没干。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I just tried to launch it but failed."
turns.zh: “我只是尝试推出它，但失败了。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And you are neither given a promotion in the company, nor a new company will say, "Oh my God, I'm going to hire this talent."
turns.zh: 而你既不会在公司里得到晋升，也不会有新的公司说“天哪，我要招这个人才”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So the guy who stayed on this stable brand within the CPG company kept growing, but that has natural tailwinds.
turns.zh: 所以，那个留在快消公司里经营稳定品牌的人持续成长，而那是有天然顺风（有利条件）的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: All he has to do is nothing in that brand.
turns.zh: 他在这个品牌上什么都不用做。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And then suddenly what you see is that he or she's managed to do well and this guy has done a zero to one has not done well.
turns.zh: 然后你突然发现，他或她经营得很好，而那个做从 0 到 1 的人却没做好。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So we do not celebrate risk-takers as a country yet.
turns.zh: 所以我们作为一个国家，还没有学会颂扬冒险者。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think we'll change that.
turns.zh: 而我认为我们会改变这一点。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think it's changing already, but we have a long way to go.
turns.zh: 我认为这已经在改变，但我们还有很长的路要走。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: One of the beautiful things I often talk about is that when I was in Portugal once and I saw, I don't know if you've ever been and seen this, but in the church normallyonly the Royalty are allowed to be buried or cremated. There is only one more category that is allowed- the explorers.
turns.zh: 我经常谈到的一件美好的事是：有一次我在葡萄牙，看到——不知道你有没有见过——在教堂里，通常只有王室才被允许安葬或火化。只有另一类人被允许——探险家。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Vasco da Gama, all of these guys who explored the world and took risks and took the country forward, were given the same position as the royalty.
turns.zh: 瓦斯科·达·伽马，所有这些探索世界、承担风险、推动国家前进的人，都被给予了与王室同等的地位。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So when we give the highest status to risk-takers, the country appreciates it because ultimately we're all looking for markers of social validation.
turns.zh: 所以当我们给冒险者最高的地位时，国家会认可这一点，因为归根结底，我们都在寻找社会认同的标志。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Super interesting.
turns.zh: 太有意思了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I want to keep talking about India and how it's different and especially what may surprise people about the market, both building there and then how to build products that are successful in India.
turns.zh: 我想继续聊印度、它有何不同，尤其是这个市场可能让人惊讶的地方——无论是在那里创业，还是如何打造在印度成功的产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I saw in a different interview, you talk about how there's this big difference between DAUs and ARPUs. In India it's really easy to get DAUs, basically get lots of users, it's really hard to make revenue per user, and that changes the way you build products broadly.
turns.zh: 我在另一个采访里看到，你谈到 DAU 和 ARPU 之间有很大的差异。在印度，获取 DAU（日活用户）、也就是获得大量用户非常容易，但要从每用户身上赚钱却非常难，而这从整体上改变了你打造产品的方式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Could you just talk about why this is the case?
turns.zh: 你能谈谈为什么会是这样吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Why is it so much easier to get DAUs versus ARPUs?
turns.zh: 为什么获取 DAU 比提升 ARPU 容易这么多？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think ARPU is a function of per capita income of a country.
turns.zh: 我认为 ARPU 是一个国家人均收入的函数。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You cannot make $100 per user from a country for a product when their income is let's say $2,500 per year as an average for the whole country.
turns.zh: 当一国的人均年收入平均只有 2500 美元时，你不可能从每个用户身上赚到 100 美元。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So what happens is many global companies love to come to India because we have the cheapest data, and very high smartphone penetration.
turns.zh: 所以发生的情况是，许多全球公司喜欢来印度，因为我们有最便宜的数据流量和非常高的智能手机普及率。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So if you look at a lot of global giants, they'll have 500 million users from India, sometimes a billion users coming from Asia and they don't have huge ARPUs, but they help you show the user growth which helps you in your public market and therefore improves your valuations.
turns.zh: 所以如果你看很多全球巨头，他们在印度有 5 亿用户，有时来自亚洲的用户达 10 亿，他们的 ARPU 并不高，但这些用户增长能帮你在公开市场上展示增长，从而提高你的估值。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, my guess is that, I don't know if this data is public or not to talk about, my guess is that Meta would not have more than $3 or $4 per user per year monetization in India.
turns.zh: 比如，我猜——不知道这个数据是否公开——Meta 在印度每用户每年的变现应该不超过 3 到 4 美元。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But if you look at the user growth in India, it is huge.
turns.zh: 但如果你看印度的用户增长，那是巨大的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So a lot of times for global companies, India becomes a great MAU farm but very low on ARPU. Therefore a lot of Indian founders who tried to copy the Western market saying, “I'm going to have a few hundred million users” make a terrible mistake because they will need to then go abroad to find their ARPUs to balance the act.
turns.zh: 所以很多时候对全球公司来说，印度变成一个很好的 MAU（月活）农场，但 ARPU 极低。因此很多印度创始人试图复制西方市场、说“我要拥有几亿用户”，就犯了一个可怕的错误，因为他们之后得去国外寻找 ARPU 来平衡。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You talk about how Netflix is a good example of that, where they launched in India, they got lots of users, but just couldn't make a lot of money.
turns.zh: 你谈到 Netflix 就是一个很好的例子——他们在印度上线，获得了大量用户，但就是赚不到多少钱。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 对。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Because forusers to find relevant content, pay for content, when we have tons of free data, tons of free content all over the place, like short videos that are competing with time, so much going on over here, people actually paying for that by design is going to be less.
turns.zh: 因为对用户来说，在我们有大量免费数据、到处都是免费内容（比如与用户时间竞争的海量短视频）、各种事情都在发生的情况下，去找到相关内容、为内容付费，人们真正愿意为此付钱的设计下，付费意愿会更低。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I'm not saying that it'll not change in 10, 20 years, but the expectation that many global companies come over here saying that, “I'm going to have these tens of millions of users who start paying me as soon as I come”, for Spotify, for Netflix, or Amazon Prime for that matter has not panned out.
turns.zh: 我并不是说 10 年、20 年后这不会改变，但很多全球公司带着“我一来，就有几千万用户马上开始给我付费”的期待来到这里——无论是 Spotify、Netflix，还是 Amazon Prime——这种期待都没有实现。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So one of my takeaways here is just when you look at a startup as an investor especially, and you see “We've got 100 million users,” don't treat that the same as say 100 million users in the US or other markets.
turns.zh: 所以我这里的一个结论是：尤其当你作为投资者看一家创业公司、看到“我们已经有 1 亿用户”时，不要把它和美国或其他市场的 1 亿用户等同看待。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 完全正确。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: One more thing is the value of time as a concept.
turns.zh: 还有一件事，是关于“时间的价值”这个概念。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So one of the things you'll notice, Lenny, is that no Indian has ever been paid an hourly salary in their entire life.
turns.zh: Lenny，你会发现的一件事是：没有一个印度人一生中拿过小时工资。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But let me ask you a question.
turns.zh: 但让我问你一个问题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What was your first ever job and how were you paid?
turns.zh: 你的第一份工作是什么，你是怎么拿报酬的？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: My first ever job, I was tutoring women about computers and passing Microsoft certification tests.
turns.zh: 我的第一份工作，是辅导女性使用电脑并通过微软认证考试。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I was paid, I'm pretty sure it was hourly.
turns.zh: 我的报酬，我相当确定是按时计算的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Now most likely you'll remember what the hour rate income was.
turns.zh: 现在你很可能还记得那个时薪是多少。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And even though you've started making a lot more, you still have the concept of what the value of your one hour is.
turns.zh: 而且即使你后来赚得多了很多，你依然对“自己一小时的价值”有概念。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But if you ask most Indians, and if you ever come to India and do this exercise when you meet them, ask them “What's your income per day or income per hour?”
turns.zh: 但如果你去问大多数印度人——如果你来印度，见到他们时做这个练习，问他们“你每天/每小时的收入是多少？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Nobody will be able to answer, no matter what their job is.
turns.zh: 没人能答得上来，无论他们做什么工作。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They could be staff, at the restaurant, to somebody who's doing really basic work, to anybody in any fancy job, because we've never ever been paid an hourly salary.
turns.zh: 他们可能是餐厅员工、做着非常基础工作的人，也可能是任何光鲜职位的人，因为我们从未拿过小时工资。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So when you're not paid an hourly salary, the concept of time is not the same.
turns.zh: 所以当你不是按小时拿工资时，对时间的概念就不一样了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And when the concept of time is not the same, paying for time is hard to do.
turns.zh: 而当对时间的概念不一样时，为时间付费就变得很难。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore you'll see a lot of Indians who make, let's say, I don't know, maybe $100 an hour, but still spend an hour to spend $10 on a flight ticket because that's what it is.
turns.zh: 所以你会看到很多印度人，比如赚着可能 100 美元一小时，却愿意花一个小时去省下 10 美元机票钱，因为就是这样。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you discuss that with many of the Indians in the West also you'll realize that this is a common joke that they will still fight for the $10 because the value of time is something that is harder to get used to unless from your childhood the unit of time was moved smaller and smaller.
turns.zh: 如果你和很多在西方生活的印度人聊这个，你会发现这是一个常见的玩笑：他们还是会为了 10 美元去争，因为时间的价值是很难习惯的，除非你从小就把时间单位切得越来越小。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That is really interesting.
turns.zh: 那真的很有意思。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And you're saying that comes from just the fact that people never get paid hourly?
turns.zh: 你的意思是，这仅仅源于人们从未拿过小时工资？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's always a salary, and so people don't write down-
turns.zh: 一直都是月薪，所以人们不会去记录——

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The concept of valuing time.
turns.zh: “对时间进行估值的这种概念。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Many Indian languages do not have a word for “efficiency.”
turns.zh: 许多印度语言里没有“效率”这个词。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that's true for many Asian languages, the word for “efficiency” does not exist.
turns.zh: 而且很多亚洲语言都是这样，“效率”这个词并不存在。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So then how do you value it if it's not in the vocabulary?
turns.zh: 所以如果词汇表里没有它，你又怎么去估量它呢？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Fascinating.
turns.zh: 太迷人了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's something else along these lines of DAUs and ARPUs and efficiency that you talked about that I love, which is this idea that focus is a curse in Asian markets, that in the US there's often this advice.
turns.zh: 沿着你谈到的 DAU、ARPU 和效率这条线，还有另一件我喜欢的事，就是“在亚洲市场，专注反而是一种诅咒”这个观点——在美国，经常有这样的建议。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: “Focus, build one thing that's amazing that everyone loves, try to make that work, scale that, and then, only then, build a new product or build something, build a new big feature.”
turns.zh: “专注，打造一个每个人都喜欢的惊艳产品，努力让它成功、把它做大，然后——只有到那时——再去打造新产品，或者做新的大功能。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And your advice is in India and Asian markets in general, it's the opposite.
turns.zh: 而你的建议是，在印度乃至整个亚洲市场，恰恰相反。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I think it's because you make so little per user.
turns.zh: 而我认为这是因为你从每用户身上赚得太少了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Could you talk about that?
turns.zh: 你能展开谈谈吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 可以。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think one is you make very little per user, so you have to do many things.
turns.zh: 我认为一是你从每用户身上赚得很少，所以你必须做很多事情。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But also all low trust markets, and let me define low trust markets as where consumers are a lot more wary of trying new things because there are no institutions that protect you against bad behavior done by a company.
turns.zh: 但还有一点，所有低信任市场——我把低信任市场定义为：消费者尝试新事物的警惕性高得多，因为没有机构能保护你免受公司的不良行为侵害。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So for example, if I ever had a fall in a coffee shop in the US, I can think about suing them and making money off it.
turns.zh: 比如，如果我在美国的咖啡店摔倒了，我会想着起诉他们并从中赚钱。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: In India, you're only worried about “I'm going to pay for my thing.”
turns.zh: 在印度，你只担心“我要为自己的东西付钱”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You don't even think about suing the coffee shop or even hoping that you'll get any money for that.
turns.zh: 你甚至不会想到起诉咖啡店，也不会指望能拿到任何赔偿。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So what happens is in a low trust country, and all developing nations are low trust by design, because the institutions are not strong enough to really, really take care of many things.
turns.zh: 所以在低信任国家——所有发展中国家本质上都是低信任的，因为制度还不够强大，无法真正照管方方面面——会发生什么呢。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What happens is there is concentration of trust.
turns.zh: 发生的是信任的集中。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So you will see that super apps, superstars, super companies all exist in low trust markets because the lack of trust creates concentration of trust, and therefore you will see one app can do 400 things.
turns.zh: 所以你会看到超级应用、超级明星、超级公司都存在于低信任市场，因为缺乏信任反而导致了信任的集中，因此你会看到一个 App 可以做 400 件事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, we have a company like Tata that can do salt to car to jewelry to anything and people will buy it because it's a Tata brand, because it comes from a low trust society trusting the brand and not being, “Oh, I'm going to prefer this new brand.”
turns.zh: 比如，我们有像塔塔（Tata）这样的公司，从盐到汽车到珠宝再到任何东西都能做，人们会买，因为它是塔塔品牌——因为它来自一个低信任社会，人们信任这个品牌，而不是“噢，我更偏好这个新品牌”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The joy of trying new things is not so high in low trust nations.
turns.zh: 在低信任国家，尝试新事物的乐趣并不高。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow, I'm learning a lot here.
turns.zh: 哇，我在这里学到了很多。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I didn't know all this.
turns.zh: 我之前都不知道这些。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So essentially the brand is even more, exponentially more important in Indian markets.
turns.zh: 所以本质上，品牌在印度市场里甚至重要得多，呈指数级地更重要。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's funny, but the oldest brand in the world is a brand called Chyavanprash.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，世界上最古老的品牌叫 Chyavanprash（恰万普拉什）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's a guy named Chavan who built a “prash” which is a sort of paste that you can have for good health, and it was built in India many, many, many, many centuries ago.
turns.zh: 是一个叫 Chavan 的人做出了一种“prash”——就是一种可以食用、有益健康的糊状物，它是在很多很多世纪以前的印度被做出来的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And lots of Indian businesses still have the name of the person behind it.
turns.zh: 而且很多印度企业至今仍带有其背后人物的名字。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Even the US is like that.
turns.zh: 美国其实也是这样。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: JP Morgan, all these guys are not some fancy name.
turns.zh: 摩根大通（JP Morgan），这些都不是什么花哨的名字。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They're the names of people.
turns.zh: 它们就是人的名字。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore in India, trust still comes from a lot of names of people who had a lot of trust behind them and reputation behind them.
turns.zh: 所以在印度，信任至今仍来自许多背后有巨大信任和声誉的人物名字。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I want to zoom out a little bit before we go in a different direction.
turns.zh: 在切换话题之前，我想稍微拉远一点视野。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: What do you see as either the most pressing challenges in India right now for tech and/or the biggest opportunity for Indian startups?
turns.zh: 你认为印度科技领域当前最紧迫的挑战是什么，和/或印度创业公司最大的机会是什么？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And then just generally where do you think things will evolve in the next few years?
turns.zh: 然后总体上，你认为未来几年事情会如何演变？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Sometimes I wonder if the challenges and the opportunities are exactly the same.
turns.zh: 有时我在想，挑战和机遇会不会其实是同一件事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, one of the biggest challenges we have is, we have very low female participation of labor compared to many markets.
turns.zh: 比如，我们最大的挑战之一是，与许多市场相比，我们的女性劳动参与率非常低。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I also believe it's an opportunity because you can, let's say, use AI and create many new types of business and opportunities because now work from home is not an alien concept anymore.
turns.zh: 但我也认为这是个机会，因为你可以——比如——利用 AI 创造许多新型业务和机会，毕竟现在居家办公已经不再是陌生的概念。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You can actually create very interesting businesses for that.
turns.zh: 你实际上可以为这点创造出非常有趣的业务。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Number two is we are low on per capita income.
turns.zh: 第二，我们的人均收入偏低。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So what AI can do instead of taking our jobs away, is just make us brighter.
turns.zh: 所以 AI 能做的，与其说是抢走我们的工作，不如说是让我们更聪明。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Satya talks about how expertise is now available in the air. So you can actually just ride on that and really make the world very equal in many many ways.
turns.zh: 萨提亚（Satya）谈到，专业知识现在“在空气中”随处可得。所以你其实可以借力于此，在许多方面真正让世界变得非常平等。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So that's a massive opportunity and also a challenge, because I often make this joke that the largest employer of the world is ‘inefficiency’, and if you take that away too quickly, we'll have a very, very jobless world.
turns.zh: 所以这是一个巨大的机会，也是一个挑战，因为我常开这样一个玩笑：世界上最大的雇主是“低效”，如果你太快把它拿走，我们将会有一个非常、非常没有工作机会的世界。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So the thing is that it can be an opportunity for a country like India and also potentially a threat because if we don't start becoming great at AI.
turns.zh: 所以问题在于，对印度这样的国家来说，它既可能是机会，也潜在是威胁——如果我们不开始精通 AI 的话。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I was actually just telling somebody today that maybe all of our interviews should be about giving a task that they can only perform if they are very good at AI.
turns.zh: 其实我今天刚跟人说，也许我们所有的面试都该围绕这样一个任务：只有非常精通 AI 的人才能完成的任务。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And no matter what the job is, you make that the minimum criteria that if they cannot use that, leverage that, they'll become a liability in 5 years anyways.
turns.zh: 而且无论是什么岗位，你都把它设为最低标准：如果他们不会使用、不会借力 AI，那五年后他们也会成为负担。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the last one is, we have a very young demographic, very well positioned with access to technology, access to smartphones and so on and so forth, a lot of hunger.
turns.zh: 最后一点是，我们的人口结构非常年轻，能接触到技术、智能手机等等，处于很好的位置，而且充满渴望。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But our challenge is that it's also the first generation that is truly learning what entrepreneurship is, what risk is, and we'll make all sorts of mistakes to get there.
turns.zh: 但我们的挑战在于，这也是真正在学习什么是创业、什么是风险的第一代人，我们会在这个过程中犯各种各样的错误。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I hope we don't go into a shell after having these large scale failures that we have not seen before.
turns.zh: 我希望我们在经历了前所未见的大规模失败后，不要缩回壳里。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: India is not used to layoffs.
turns.zh: 印度还不习惯裁员。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Like the startup world is used to layoffs, but in India, if startups do layoffs, it becomes the national news and all sorts of discussions happen over here.
turns.zh: 创业圈习惯了裁员，但在印度，如果创业公司裁员，就会变成全国新闻，引发各种讨论。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So we are not there yet.
turns.zh: 所以我们还没到那个阶段。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So we are stuck between being somewhat of a collectivist or somewhat of an individualistic society.
turns.zh: 所以我们夹在某种集体主义社会和某种个人主义社会之间。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We are somewhere.
turns.zh: 我们处于中间位置。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: India is a great remix of everything.
turns.zh: 印度是万物的大融合。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love this line you just shared of “inefficiencies is the largest employer in the world”.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢你刚才分享的那句话——“低效是世界上最大的雇主”。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I totally get that.
turns.zh: 我完全理解。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So let's talk about CRED for a bit.
turns.zh: 那么我们聊聊 CRED 吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So you had, I think three startups before CRED?
turns.zh: 在 CRED 之前，你有过——我想是三家创业公司？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And then you've been building CRED for about six years now.
turns.zh: 然后你打造 CRED 到现在大约六年了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm curious just on this journey of CRED, what you've learned or changed your mind about, during this phase of your career versus previous phases.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，在 CRED 的这段旅程中，与你之前的阶段相比，你学到了什么、又改变了哪些看法。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think CRED's insight was actually quite simple.
turns.zh: 我认为 CRED 的洞察其实相当简单。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We realized that unfortunately the value of time and per capita income is concentrated with 25 million families and therefore focusing on them is important.
turns.zh: 我们意识到，不幸的是，时间和人均收入的价值集中在 2500 万个家庭手中，因此聚焦他们是非常重要的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And they are a lot more global in their approach versus the rest of India.
turns.zh: 而且他们的方式比印度其他群体要全球化得多。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So you have to build for them very differently.
turns.zh: 所以你必须非常不同地针对他们去做产品。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I realized that the ability to focus on a customer set, which is not historically possible to do because every investor expected us to be the next China, and the only similarity of India and China was the population and nothing else was similar.
turns.zh: 而且我意识到，聚焦某一客户群体的能力，在历史上是不可能的——因为每个投资者都期望我们成为“下一个中国”，而印度和中国唯一的相似点就是人口，其他什么都不像。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think having that conviction that, “I'm going to build only for these folks and this large enough market.”
turns.zh: 所以我认为，拥有这样一种信念——“我只为这些人、这个足够大的市场而建”——是很重要的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Thankfully I had one success for somebody to bet.
turns.zh: 幸好我之前有过一次成功，才有人愿意下注。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So our series A was $25 million.
turns.zh: 所以我们的 A 轮融了 2500 万美元。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I would've not had that luxury if I had no success in the past because I had no product with any monetization to prove that I'm doing the right thing.
turns.zh: 如果我过去没有成功，我不会有这种待遇，因为我没有任何能变现的产品来证明我做的是对的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It turned out okay, but I think I could get a lot of people to take a risk behind my insight or my thesis because I focused on the right customer category and built on it.
turns.zh: 结果还算不错，但我认为我能说服很多人基于我的洞察或论点去冒险，因为我聚焦在了正确的客户类别并据此构建。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I think the few things I've learned differently is that companies that are very, very good at zero to one will not naturally become great at 10 to 100.
turns.zh: 但我认为我学到的少数不同点是：非常擅长从 0 到 1 的公司，不会自然而然地擅长从 10 到 100。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: There are lots of different lessons to learn.
turns.zh: 还有很多不同的经验教训要学。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The founder has to evolve.
turns.zh: 创始人必须进化。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: That’s the biggest thing that has to happen.
turns.zh: 这是必须发生的最重要的事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Most people at CRED are people who have not seen a bigger business than CRED, which comes with its benefits and costs.
turns.zh: CRED 里大多数人没见过比 CRED 更大的业务，这有好处也有代价。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So you have to gentrify the org every now and then to make people understand the value of many of these reliable things.
turns.zh: 所以你得时不时地“升级”组织，让人们理解那些可靠事物的价值。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I often tell people that entrepreneurs are uncertainty absorbers for everybody- for employees, for investors, for customers- and therefore they get rewarded for being those people who remove uncertainty from people's lives.
turns.zh: 而且我常跟人说，创业者是每个人的“不确定性吸收器”——为员工、为投资者、为客户——因此他们得到回报，正是因为他们是那些消除人们生活中不确定性的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But the kind of expectations keep changing at companies of scale.
turns.zh: 但到了一定规模的公司，外界的期望也在不断变化。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, if you have, let's say a seed stage investor, they are very used to very high uncertainty and they're happy with some absorption.
turns.zh: 比如，如果你有种子轮投资者，他们非常习惯高度不确定性，也乐于看到你吸收一些。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But as you get a growth investor, and let's say you have sovereigns on your cap table, the amount of stability you need to provide is significantly more, and therefore you need to evolve very, very differently.
turns.zh: 但当你有了成长型投资者，假设你的股东名册上还有主权基金，你需要提供的稳定性就显著更高，因此你需要以非常非常不同的方式进化。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think those are the few lessons that I've learned.
turns.zh: 所以我认为这些就是我学到的一些教训。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Talent, you start realizing that not everybody can scale into everything.
turns.zh: 关于人才，你开始意识到并非每个人都能扩展到所有领域。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And you cannot expect that you can give up the 0 to 1 DNA just because you're building 10 to 100.
turns.zh: 而且你不能因为正在做从 10 到 100，就指望可以放弃从 0 到 1 的 DNA。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So how do you kind of coexist with those things?
turns.zh: 那么如何与这些事情共存呢？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: How do you react to big changes in the market and not become this slow company?
turns.zh: 你如何对市场的大变化做出反应，而不变成一家迟钝的公司？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And every company goes through that.
turns.zh: 每家公司都会经历这些。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I mean if you look at what Zuck went through in the last three or four years was that.
turns.zh: 我的意思是，你看小扎（Zuck）过去三四年经历的正是这个。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I often say that he had to play the Shiva, come and do a lot of destruction to become big again.
turns.zh: 我常说，他必须扮演湿婆（Shiva），通过大量的毁灭才能再次变大。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think that's what founders can do, and it's not easy to do.
turns.zh: 所以我认为这就是创始人能做的事，而且这并不容易。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: One of the things I've learned is that profit pools of a country tell you a lot about what the country values.
turns.zh: 我学到的一件事是，一个国家的利润池（profit pools）能告诉你很多关于这个国家看重什么的信息。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And trying to copy somebody else's profit pool to your country will not be a wise idea because the country's values are demonstrated in what profit pools exist.
turns.zh: 试图把别人的利润池复制到自己的国家并不是一个明智的主意，因为这个国家看重什么，就体现在存在哪些利润池上。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Let's take an example.
turns.zh: 举个例子。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: In the thousand most profitable companies in India, the number of retailers would be probably two or three.
turns.zh: 在印度最赚钱的 1000 家公司里，零售商可能只有两三家。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But if you look at the Western market, you'll see a bunch of them because it's a consumption market, plus a very high divorce rate which means you're always peacocking again in the market, you're trying to be fit and be cool and all of that.
turns.zh: 但如果你看西方市场，你会看到一大堆，因为那是一个消费市场，加上极高的离婚率意味着你总在市场中再次“开屏炫耀”（peacocking），努力保持身材、显得酷，诸如此类。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: India has a very low divorce rate, less than 1%, are arranged marriages.
turns.zh: 印度的离婚率很低，不到 1%，而且是包办婚姻。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Fashion spends, and because we have a lower female participation of labor, India is probably the only market where female fashion spends is less than men's fashion spends.
turns.zh: 关于时尚消费，由于我们女性劳动参与率较低，印度可能是唯一一个女性时尚消费低于男性时尚消费的市场。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Everywhere else, it's probably five, 6x more for them.
turns.zh: 在其他地方，女性在这方面的消费大概是男性的 5 到 6 倍。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So what happens is you start appreciating what the country values.
turns.zh: 所以发生的是，你开始理解这个国家看重什么。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, I have noticed that many patriarchal societies have a very significant market cap in financial services versus consumption.
turns.zh: 比如，我注意到许多父权社会在金融服务（而非消费）上拥有非常显著的市值占比。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And these broad patterns, you start thinking about very, very differently.
turns.zh: 而这些宏观规律，会让你以一种非常不同的方式去思考。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So many lessons there.
turns.zh: 那里有太多经验教训了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love this idea of a founder being an uncertainty absorber.
turns.zh: 我很喜欢“创始人是不确定性吸收器”这个观点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This other point you made about Zuck becoming the Shiva and destruction touches on something Brian Chesky and I chatted a bit about, how founders often start in control, very micromanaging, just driving the ship.
turns.zh: 你提到的另一点——小扎扮演湿婆进行毁灭——触及了我和 Brian Chesky 聊过的一些内容，即创始人通常如何以掌控、极度微观管理、亲自掌舵开始。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And then as the company grows, they delegate and empower and then things start to slow down and then they come back, play the Shiva and take control again.
turns.zh: 然后随着公司成长，他们放权、赋能，但之后事情开始变慢，于是他们又回来，扮演湿婆，重新掌控。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything there that you've seen-
turns.zh: 你有没有看到过什么相关的——

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Yeah, but that's the universe.
turns.zh: 是的，但那就是宇宙的规律。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The universe goes through the exact same phases.
turns.zh: 宇宙经历的正是完全相同的阶段。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So if you study Indian mythology, you'll see that there's a Brahma, Vishnu, Mahesh cycles and every yugg As it’s called, goes through these three phases all the time.
turns.zh: 所以如果你研究印度神话，你会看到梵天、毗湿奴、马赫什（Mahesh，即湿婆）的循环，而每一个所谓的“纪元”（yuga）都始终经历这三个阶段。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Beautiful.
turns.zh: 太美了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I see.
turns.zh: 我明白了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So this is just inevitable.
turns.zh: 所以这就是不可避免的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is the circle of life.
turns.zh: 这就是生命的循环。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Absolutely.
turns.zh: 确实如此。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing.
turns.zh: 太妙了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love how this all just ties back to your philosophy background.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这一切如何又回到你的哲学背景上。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love it.
turns.zh: 我喜欢。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's beautiful.
turns.zh: 太美了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This episode is brought to you by Dovetail, the customer insights hub for product teams.
turns.zh: 本期节目由 Dovetail 赞助，它是面向产品团队的客户洞察中心。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Are you working in a feature factory building filler that nobody wants?
turns.zh: 你是不是在一家“功能工厂”里，打造着没人想要的东西？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Probably, because the sad truth is that most SaaS features are rarely or never used, costing the industry billions every year.
turns.zh: 很可能是，因为可悲的真相是：大多数 SaaS 功能很少被使用，甚至从未被使用，每年让行业损失数十亿。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Let's change that.
turns.zh: 让我们改变这一点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Product managers, Dovetail is holding their first industry conference, it's called Insight Out, and they want you to come over one day in San Francisco.
turns.zh: 产品经理们，Dovetail 正在举办他们的首届行业大会，名为 Insight Out，他们希望你能来旧金山参加为期一天的活动。

turns.zh: 产品社区将齐聚一堂，学习如何更好地利用客户洞察，打造人们真正爱用的产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's on April 11, and you can hear from product leaders from Uber, Twitch Meta and Netflix as they share their strategies for driving innovation, thriving in uncertainty and balancing customer centered work with business needs.
turns.zh: 大会在 4 月 11 日举行，你可以听到来自 Uber、Twitch、Meta 和 Netflix 的产品领导者分享他们推动创新、在不确定的环境中蓬勃发展、以及平衡以客户为中心的工作与业务需求的策略。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And here's the kicker, it's absolutely free for online tickets.
turns.zh: 而最棒的是，线上门票完全免费。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just go to dovetail.com/lenny to register.
turns.zh: 只需前往 dovetail.com/lenny 注册。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is thanks to Dovetail, the best way for product teams to get the most out of customer insights.
turns.zh: 感谢 Dovetail，它是产品团队最大化利用客户洞察的最佳方式。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Check it out at dovetail.com/lenny.
turns.zh: 前往 dovetail.com/lenny 了解。
