turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So, on CRED.
turns.zh: 那么，关于 CRED。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So here's a funny thing that happened.
turns.zh: 这里发生了一件有趣的事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I asked people on Twitter what questions to ask you on this podcast, and one of the most common questions was “When do you think you'll become profitable?”
turns.zh: 我在 Twitter 上问大家，在这档播客里该问你什么问题，而最常见的问题之一是“你认为你们什么时候能实现盈利？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Which is interesting because when I have other CEOs that are founding a company that is, and most companies aren't profitable, nobody's asking that question.
turns.zh: 这很有意思，因为当我采访其他 CEO、创办一家（大多数公司都不盈利的）公司时，没人问这个问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So I'm just curious, why is that such a common question that comes up?
turns.zh: 所以我只是好奇，为什么这会是一个如此常见的问题？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's fascinating.
turns.zh: 太有意思了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's fascinating.
turns.zh: 太有意思了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: As a country, most businesses were of trading, you buy something at low cost, sell at a higher price and you make profit.
turns.zh: 作为一个国家，我们大多数生意都是贸易型的——你低价买入，高价卖出，从而获利。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Most of our businesses, most of our family businesses were trading.
turns.zh: 我们大多数生意、大多数家族企业都是做贸易的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But building a CapEx heavy distribution, monetizing it later on, focusing on high revenue growth rate versus trying to get profitability first, is not known to us.
turns.zh: 但建立重资本支出（CapEx）的分销体系、之后再变现、重视营收高速增长而非先追求盈利——这对我们来说并不熟悉。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So when they see these large numbers of losses, there's a shock. “Why would somebody give you this kind of money?”
turns.zh: 所以当人们看到这些巨大的亏损数字时，会大吃一惊。“为什么会有人给你这么多钱？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And by the way, my own dad wouldn't respect me till I was building a profitable company.
turns.zh: 而且，顺便说一句，在我做出一家盈利的公司之前，我自己的父亲都不会尊重我。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So it's not surprising that people in India have these comments, but it also comes from not understanding how businesses are built in the internet world, where VCs are giving you the capital to build distribution, unique product edge, brand, all of that stuff, and then monetize later on and monetize big and then have very large profit pools to go after.
turns.zh: 所以印度人有这些评论并不奇怪，但这也源于他们不了解互联网世界里的企业是如何建立的——VC 给你资本去建立分销网络、独特的产品优势、品牌等等，然后再变现、大规模变现，进而追逐非常巨大的利润池。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But a lot of times this comes from not understanding this business, and I feel it'll change because many internet companies are now getting very profitable and public listed.
turns.zh: 但很多时候这源于对这门生意的不理解，而我觉得这会改变，因为现在很多互联网公司正变得非常盈利并上市。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So we'll have a decade.
turns.zh: 所以我们将有（见证这一切的）十年时间。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Let's understand one thing.
turns.zh: 让我们理解一件事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: In the US, maybe 27-30% of the US market cap is now tech companies.
turns.zh: 在美国，现在大约 27% 到 30% 的市值来自科技公司。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: In India tech companies would probably make less than 2- 3% of the market cap.
turns.zh: 在印度，科技公司可能只占市值的不到 2% 到 3%。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So we are mostly, and I'm not saying India has this fabulous history of building very, very profitable tech companies.
turns.zh: 所以我们基本上……我并不是说印度有打造非常盈利的科技公司的辉煌历史。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We are probably the first generation that will have to prove ourselves to be very large profitable companies.
turns.zh: 我们很可能是需要证明自己能成为非常大型盈利公司的第一代。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But we are still figuring out what this means.
turns.zh: 但我们仍在摸索这意味着什么。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the fact that this question, by the way, I can tell you one thing that, I have been asked this question by people on Twitter way more than any of my investors have ever asked me this question. This also creates an arbitrage for entrepreneurs who can actually build businesses and have the ability to raise capital and prove their business model with very high revenue growth rate and build large brands and so on and so forth.
turns.zh: 而且关于这个问题，我可以告诉你一件事：我在 Twitter 上被问到这个问题的次数，远超任何一位投资者问过我的次数。这也为那些真正能建立业务、有能力融资、以极高营收增速验证商业模式、并打造大品牌等的创业者创造了套利空间。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I find it fascinating as well.
turns.zh: 但我也觉得这很迷人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Also, one thing we see fascinating in India is that there is an immense amount of trolling and doubt that will come in your comments no matter what you do.
turns.zh: 还有，我们在印度看到一件迷人的事：无论你做什么，评论区都会涌来海量的嘲讽和质疑。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So if you see any founder in India, they'll post something about the thing, the comments will rarely have appreciation.
turns.zh: 所以如果你看印度任何一位创始人发的动态，评论里几乎不会有赞赏。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So it feels sad because, when you see global companies do stuff, Indians will lose their shit on Apple Vision Pro and all this stuff and Twitter will go gaga over it.
turns.zh: 这让人感觉挺难过，因为当全球公司推出东西时，印度人会对 Apple Vision Pro 之类的东西大加赞赏，Twitter 也会为之疯狂。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I think when it comes to...and I believe envy is hyperlocal.
turns.zh: 但我认为当涉及到……而且我相信嫉妒是高度本地化的（hyperlocal）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We do not envy Elon Musk for all the stuff he does because he's so far away.
turns.zh: 我们不会嫉妒埃隆·马斯克做的那些事，因为他离得太远了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But we envy our own because they were just like us not many years ago.
turns.zh: 但我们会嫉妒自己人，因为他们几年前还和我们一样。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore envy is like wifi.
turns.zh: 所以嫉妒就像 wifi。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's like a hyperlocal service.
turns.zh: 它就像一种本地化服务。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: How do you stay positive and focused and not let that stuff bring you down?
turns.zh: 你如何保持积极和专注，不被这些东西击垮？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And do you have advice for founders in India that are dealing with the same sort of feedback?
turns.zh: 你对正在面对同样反馈的印度创始人有什么建议吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's funny the number of calls I've got from founders who start getting hate. I’m the go-to person to get these call because they've seen me get it for many more years.
turns.zh: 有意思的是，多少创始人一开始收到仇恨言论就会给我打电话。我是他们求助的首选，因为他们看到我承受这些已经很多年了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I tell people that we couldn't have made it this far if we cared about criticism of everybody versus people who've done better than us.
turns.zh: 而我告诉人们：如果我们在意每个人的批评，而不是那些比我们做得更好的人的批评，我们不可能走到今天这一步。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: If somebody who's done anything better than me gives me any amount of criticism, I will absolutely flip and make all the changes and evolve.
turns.zh: 如果某个在任何方面比我做得好的人给我任何批评，我绝对会彻底改变、做出所有调整并进化。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I seek feedback all the time from people.
turns.zh: 而且我一直向人们寻求反馈。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But if I start taking feedback from everybody who does not understand the nuance and empathize with what I'm doing, I'm not saying that we should not take customer feedback, that's very different.
turns.zh: 但如果我开始听取每一个不理解其中细微差别、也不同情我所做之事的人的反馈——我并不是说我们不该听取客户反馈，那是完全不同的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But let's say somebody commenting about your business, who does not understand the nuance of it, you can't be reacting to everything.
turns.zh: 但假设有人在评论你的业务，却不懂其中的微妙之处，你不可能对一切都做出反应。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I often tell people that there's a reason elements with lower valencies are called noble gases because they're hardest to get reactions from.
turns.zh: 而且我常跟人说，化合价低的元素被称为惰性气体是有原因的，因为它们最难发生反应。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's over my head, but I love it anyway.
turns.zh: 这超出我的理解范围了，但我还是喜欢。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's so interesting.
turns.zh: 这太有趣了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love all these elements you're pointing out of how different building in India is. I think people in the US have no idea about it.
turns.zh: 我喜欢你指出的所有这些关于在印度创业有多不同的点。我认为美国人对这些一无所知。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so I appreciate you getting into all these little elements.
turns.zh: 所以我感谢你深入探讨了所有这些小细节。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything else around the Indian market that may surprise people before we go in a different direction about building a startup there?
turns.zh: 在换话题聊在那里创业之前，关于印度市场还有什么可能让人惊讶的地方吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For all the challenges, India remains the most promising market that one can be building for right now because everything is going our way.
turns.zh: 尽管有种种挑战，印度依然是目前最值得为之创业的市场，因为一切都在朝我们这边发展。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We have all sorts of digital public infrastructure, government support, all these great people doing extraordinary things, apart from the Twitter noise.
turns.zh: 我们拥有各种各样的数字公共基础设施、政府支持，还有所有这些做出非凡成就的优秀人才——除了 Twitter 上的噪音之外。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And Twitter is designed for outrage getting likes.
turns.zh: 而且 Twitter 本身就是为了煽动愤怒、获取点赞而设计的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I wouldn't read too much into it.
turns.zh: 所以我不会太把它当回事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I think all of us are doing well because we have an audience set, an evolved ecosystem that is fully supporting us and really taking it forward.
turns.zh: 但我认为我们所有人都做得很好，因为我们有一群受众、一个成熟的生态系统在全力支持我们，并真正推动它向前发展。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think I wouldn't want to be anywhere else in building because of this extremely vibrant, crazy opportunity that one can learn from.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，正因为有这种极其活跃、疯狂的机会可以从中学习，我哪儿都不想去创业。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: However, I often wish that I could get a one month internship with Brian and learn how to do things.
turns.zh: 不过，我常常希望我能跟着 Brian 实习一个月，学学怎么做事情。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I've never had the luxury.
turns.zh: 而我从未有过这种奢侈。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I can only watch his podcast with you to learn a few things, but what if I got a chance to be there?
turns.zh: 我只能通过看他与你的播客来学点东西，但如果我有个机会亲临现场呢？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I miss that part where I've never been really trained by these extraordinary product brains or even observed them make decisions.
turns.zh: 而且我很遗憾，我从未被这些卓越的产品大脑真正训练过，甚至从未观察过他们做决策。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I recently posted one thing that the word ‘operation theater’ comes because operating used to be a public process and people used to pay money to watch surgeries and see all the bloody gory stuff and even before anesthesia was born.
turns.zh: 所以我最近发了一条：手术室（operation theater）这个词之所以存在，是因为手术曾经是一个公开的过程，人们会花钱观看手术、看到那些血淋淋的场面，甚至在麻醉发明之前就是如此。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And there's so much joy in seeing somebody do their action.
turns.zh: 而且看着别人行动本身就有很多乐趣。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I wish there was a theater for Brian taking a product decision, Zuck taking a hard call on killing a product or seeing Tim rejecting all the ideas that they have before the GTM of a product.
turns.zh: 我真希望有一个“剧场”，能看到 Brian 做产品决策、小扎艰难地决定砍掉一个产品、或者看 Tim 在产品上市（GTM）前否决他们所有的想法。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think we could benefit so much from that.
turns.zh: 我认为我们能从中受益匪浅。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And unfortunately it remains in very small circles.
turns.zh: 而不幸的是，这种东西只存在于很小的圈子里。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And like I said, the reason I said you do a fabulous job of removing some of the information asymmetry and kind of making it more democratic.
turns.zh: 就像我说的，我之所以说你做了一件了不起的事，是因为你消除了一些信息不对称，并让这一切更“民主化”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But there is so much more that we all could learn.
turns.zh: 但我们大家能学的还有太多太多。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I feel extremely envious of many people who have the opportunity to work with the best of the best because, many of us from India never had the luxury. We had to figure out everything on our own.
turns.zh: 而且我对许多有机会与最顶尖的人共事的人感到极度羡慕，因为我们许多印度人从未有过这种奢侈。我们得靠自己弄明白一切。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: How cool would that be just to have a camera in some of those meetings just as a learning experience, because very few people are in those rooms and there's so much to learn.
turns.zh: 如果能在某些会议里放一台摄像机，纯粹作为学习体验，那该多酷啊，因为没几个人能进那些房间，而且有太多值得学习的东西。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I think though people will find, “Holy shit, one, this is how decisions are made, what is going on?”
turns.zh: 但我想人们会发现：“天哪，第一，决策原来是这么做的，到底发生了什么？”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And two is , “I don't want to work for this person.
turns.zh: “第二，‘我不想为这个人工作。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This sounds very difficult and stressful.”
turns.zh: “这听起来非常困难且充满压力。’”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Those are probably some takeaways that will emerge.
turns.zh: 这些大概是会浮现出来的一些收获。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Kind of along these lines, something that comes up a lot in your talks and work is curiosity.
turns.zh: 顺着这条线，你的演讲和工作里经常出现的一个词是好奇心。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You have a show called CRED curious.
turns.zh: 你有一档节目叫 CRED Curious（CRED 好奇心）。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You often talk about the power of curiosity.
turns.zh: 你经常谈到好奇心的力量。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm just curious, why is curiosity so important to you and why is it important for other people to always stay curious and what value is there?
turns.zh: 我只是好奇，为什么好奇心对你如此重要？为什么对其他人来说保持好奇也很重要？这其中有什么价值？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think a curious person is somebody who is constantly demonstrating that they are not proud of their expertise, and they will demonstrate extraordinary amounts of excitement when they face a problem which they have no clue how to solve.
turns.zh: 我认为一个有好奇心的人，是不断在展示自己并不为自己的专业而骄傲的人，而且当他们面对一个毫无头绪、不知如何解决的问题时，会表现出极大的兴奋。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore a lot of people stop growing because they want to constantly demonstrate their expertise versus demonstrating their curiosity.
turns.zh: 因此很多人停止了成长，因为他们想不断展示自己的专业，而不是展示自己的好奇。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Because, curiosity should come from security because imagine- I'm the founder, CEO of this company and this group of 60 people on WhatsApp, somebody posts something and asks a dumb question, “What does this word mean?”
turns.zh: 因为好奇心应源于安全感——想象一下，我是这家公司的创始人兼 CEO，WhatsApp 上有个 60 人的群，有人发了一条，问了个蠢问题：“这个词是什么意思？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You need to have the security to feel okay with it, but a lot of people out off insecurity try to demonstrate expertise and do it or Google to not ask these people.
turns.zh: 你需要有安全感才能坦然接受，但很多人出于不安全感，会试图展示专业、自己去搜索，而不问这些人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think that slows down the compounding growth and I think it keeps you from being very good at adapting.
turns.zh: 而我认为这会拖慢复利式成长，也会让你无法很好地适应。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So it's funny, I was recently. GPT is my favorite thing to keep asking random questions because now I don't need to really worry about Google having those questions answered around because I can ask the GPT.
turns.zh: 所以很有趣，我最近……GPT 是我用来不断问各种随机问题的最爱，因为现在我不需要再担心 Google 能不能回答这些问题，我可以直接问 GPT。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I recently asked the question: which species or animals have survived for more than 100 million years without changing too much and what is common in all of them?
turns.zh: 所以我最近问了这样一个问题：哪些物种或动物存在了超过 1 亿年却没怎么改变？它们之间有什么共同点？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So GPT came up with an interesting answer which says that sharks, horseshoe crabs, crocodiles, and all of these animals have survived to do this thing.
turns.zh: GPT 给出了一个有趣的答案：鲨鱼、鲎（马蹄蟹）、鳄鱼，所有这些动物都做到了这一点。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So three distinct traits were, one, ability to reduce metabolism at will.
turns.zh: 所以三个鲜明的特征：第一，能够随意降低新陈代谢。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's fascinating.
turns.zh: 太迷人了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I can bring down my metabolism by 1:20 or a crazy, crazy scale that they can bring the metabolism down.
turns.zh: 它们能把新陈代谢降低 1/20，或者一个疯狂到极致的幅度。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: By the way, ancient yogis have demonstrated this as well.
turns.zh: 顺便说一句，古代瑜伽修行者也展示过这一点。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It comes from the same yogic practice.
turns.zh: 它源自同样的瑜伽修行。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The second thing is about, and if you think about companies, the context is the same.
turns.zh: 第二点是——如果你想想公司，语境是一样的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: If COVID came, you could slow down your metabolism and survive, right?
turns.zh: 如果新冠来了，你可以放慢新陈代谢并活下来，对吧？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Or you burned your way out and disappeared.
turns.zh: 或者你烧光一切然后消失。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The second thing that was interesting was the very high conversion rate on every attempt to secure food.
turns.zh: 第二件有趣的事是，它们每次获取食物都有极高的转化率。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They don't go around chasing randomly and doing things.
turns.zh: 它们不会到处乱追、瞎忙活。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They have a very high conversion rate, which means high judgment and the deadliest bite.
turns.zh: 它们有极高的转化率，这意味着高判断力和最致命的一咬。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So they'll not chase many options, but if they chase something, they will have the biggest bite and they'll convert it.
turns.zh: 所以它们不会追逐很多选项，但一旦追逐某个目标，就会给出最致命的一击并将其拿下。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the third thing that was more interesting was that they have survived all sorts of crazy environmental changes, just adapting. And adaptation comes from curiosity.
turns.zh: 而第三件更有趣的事是，它们经历了各种疯狂的环境变化都存活了下来，只是靠适应。而适应来自好奇心。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And you could see those people.
turns.zh: 而你可以看到那些人（具备这种特质的人）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: In COVID, there were two sets of people, who were completely gone into a shell and there were those who were curious.
turns.zh: 在新冠期间，有两类人：一类完全缩进了壳里，另一类是那些充满好奇的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: “Okay, so what do I do with this?”
turns.zh: “好，那我该怎么应对这个？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: “What happens now?”
turns.zh: “现在会发生什么？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: “Do I need to change something?”
turns.zh: “我需要改变什么吗？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: “Do I need to tweak something?”
turns.zh: “我需要调整什么吗？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So the ability to change very quickly.
turns.zh: 所以这种快速改变的能力。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I often feel that curiosity is that demonstration of the ability to adapt and learn, and you only create more information asymmetry.
turns.zh: 我常觉得，好奇心就是展示适应与学习的能力，而你只会借此创造更多的信息不对称。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: To me, wealth is nothing but information asymmetry.
turns.zh: 对我来说，财富不过就是信息不对称。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: All the best companies in the world have unfair information asymmetry.
turns.zh: 世界上所有最优秀的公司都拥有不公平的信息不对称。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that comes from curiosity. Because you're constantly collecting dots, connecting dots, collecting dots, connecting dots, and end up creating this unique edge for yourself and information asymmetry for yourself.
turns.zh: 而这来自好奇心。因为你不断收集点、连接点，再收集、再连接，最终为自己创造出这种独特的优势和属于自己的信息不对称。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you assume that “I have collected enough,” no human life is going to be enough to connect and connect all the dots.
turns.zh: 而如果你认为“我已经收集得够多了”，那么没有任何人的一生足够长，能把所有的点都连接起来。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We'll never be able to get..
turns.zh: 我们永远无法……

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And sometimes I envy the stuff that you do because you are efficiently connecting and collecting dots by having the luxury of all these people to talk to, and you are making more dots getting connected.
turns.zh: 而且有时我很羡慕你做的事，因为你拥有和所有这些人对谈的奢侈，高效地连接和收集着点，让更多的点连在一起。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So your information asymmetry is growing.
turns.zh: 所以你的信息不对称在增长。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wait until you IPO, and then someday maybe leave CRED and then you could start this podcast with everyone like this and connect all the dots.
turns.zh: 等你 IPO 了，也许有一天离开 CRED，然后你也可以像这样和所有人做这档播客，把所有的点连起来。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I think that's a reference to Danny Meyer who's the founder of all these fancy restaurants and big on hospitality and has this phrase “Always be collecting dots”, I think ABCD, I’ll link to that.
turns.zh: 而且我认为这指的是 Danny Meyer——那些高档餐厅的创始人，非常注重待客之道，他有一句话叫“永远在收集点”（Always be collecting dots），我想是 ABCD 法则，我会把链接放上去。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wait, this is really interesting, this list of what are the common traits of the most long-lasting animals?
turns.zh: 等等，这真的很有趣，这份关于最长寿动物共同特征的清单？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: They can lower their metabolism at will, they have a high conversion rate to get food, and they've survived many types of environments.
turns.zh: 它们能随意降低新陈代谢，获取食物时有很高的转化率，并且挺过了多种类型的环境。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And I think there's a lot you can transform as you've done, to startups and leaders.
turns.zh: 而且我认为，就像你已经做的那样，你可以把很多东西转化应用到创业公司和领导者身上。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This could be its own…
turns.zh: 这本身可以做成一篇……

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: if you haven't written about this, this would be a cool blog post.
turns.zh: 如果你还没写过这个，这会是一篇很酷的博客文章。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm curious who you look up to in business, either in India and outside India.
turns.zh: 我很好奇，在商业上你仰慕谁，无论是在印度还是印度之外。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Who comes to mind where you're like, I really inspired, I'm inspired by these folks?
turns.zh: 你会想到谁，让你觉得“我真的很受这些人启发”？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I often tell people that I hate the word ‘favorite’ because it tells me to become limited in my mind.
turns.zh: 我常跟人说，我讨厌“最喜欢”这个词，因为它会让我的思维变得局限。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I stay away from ‘favorite’, but I learn all the time from everybody.
turns.zh: 所以我远离“最喜欢”，但我一直向每个人学习。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And there are so many people to learn from across the world and in history, in the recent past and every time you'll discover fascinating, extraordinary things about them.
turns.zh: 世界上有太多人可以学习，历史中、近过去都是，每次你都会发现关于他们迷人而非凡的事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I don't think I have a person.
turns.zh: 所以我觉得我并没有某一个特定的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I am this person who thinks about about: ”How did they solve this hard problem.”
turns.zh: 我是那种会想“他们是如何解决这个难题的”的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So one of the things that we started doing recently and not very ritualistic about it so far is, I ask myself and my key reportees every month, we go around the table and ask ourselves, ”What are the hardest problems we solved last month?”
turns.zh: 所以最近我们开始做的一件事（目前还没形成固定仪式）是：我每个月会问自己和我的核心下属，大家围着桌子问自己：“上个月我们解决了哪些最难的问题？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And it's very hard to come up with an answer.
turns.zh: 而很难想出一个答案。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you do this to the product leaders, just go around and ask, “What are the hard problems you solved last month?”
turns.zh: 如果你对产品负责人也这么做，只是转一圈问问“你上个月解决了什么难题？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You'll realize that we all stay very busy and displacement is hard.
turns.zh: 你会意识到，我们都很忙，而真正的“位移”（displacement，指取得实质突破）很难。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But if you notice extraordinarily successful people, they'll have a lot more content to talk about every month, every quarter because they're obsessed with making that big displacement and it does not come by being busy.
turns.zh: 但如果你留意那些极其成功的人，他们每个月、每个季度都有更多可聊的内容，因为他们痴迷于实现那种大的“位移”，而这并不是靠忙碌得来的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that's another thing that you cannot chase the big thing.
turns.zh: 而这是另一件事——你不能去追逐那个“大东西”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You don't see a crocodile being busy.
turns.zh: 你看不到鳄鱼在“忙碌”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You see a crocodile just waiting patiently at the watering hole for that best meal and have the deadliest bite for that.
turns.zh: 你看到的是鳄鱼只是耐心地守在水坑边，等待那顿最丰盛的大餐，并为此给出最致命的一咬。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So the beautiful definition of predators I read was “one who burns the least amount of calories to earn the most amount of calories.”
turns.zh: 所以我读到过一个关于掠食者的绝妙定义：“以最少的卡路里消耗，换取最多的卡路里收入。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So how do you become that?
turns.zh: 那么你要如何成为那样的人呢？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think when I meet people who are extraordinary at that, and it comes in all shapes and forms, I learn something from them.
turns.zh: 而我认为，当我遇到在这方面极其出色的人——它以各种形式呈现——我会从他们身上学到东西。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: So in these meetings you have, are you judging people's success based on how many hard problems they solve?
turns.zh: 所以在你这些会议里，你是在根据人们解决了多少难题来判断他们的成功吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Now that they've heard this, they're going to be like, I need more.
turns.zh: 既然他们听到了这个，他们会说：我需要更多（难题）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Because if you're a senior, what is the role of a senior person?
turns.zh: 因为如果你是高管，高管的角色是什么？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You have to be the chief problem solver.
turns.zh: 你必须是首席问题解决者。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love that.
turns.zh: 我喜欢这个说法。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I often think of leaders as professional firefighters who have just endless fires to put out.
turns.zh: 我常把领导者想象成职业消防员，总有灭不完的火。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Kind of along the lines of people and where you learn from, are there any sources of content?
turns.zh: 顺着“人和你从哪里学习”这条线，你有什么内容来源吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This is actually an audience question on Twitter.
turns.zh: 这其实是 Twitter 上一个观众的问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Anurag Verma asks this, “What are your favorite sources of content to learn from in terms of what's happening in the world and what to pay attention to?”
turns.zh: Anurag Verma 问：“就了解世界上正在发生什么、以及该关注什么而言，你最喜欢用来学习的内容来源是什么？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I wish I could think of an answer.
turns.zh: 我希望我能想出个答案。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: My method of collecting information is mostly about, I come up with conjectures in my head and then I go all over the place to find out if there is proof if what I'm saying is true or not.
turns.zh: 我收集信息的方法主要是：先在脑子里提出一些猜想，然后到处去寻找证据，看我说的到底是对是错。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, I recently came up with a conjecture that everybody who has been successful in the history of business of vices, historically has done a lot of philanthropy to create a good image for themselves, and therefore is being treated as a respected citizen versus being treated as a person who did vices to make wealth.
turns.zh: 比如，我最近提出一个猜想：在历史上，所有在“恶习生意”（vices，如烟酒赌博等）上取得成功的人，都曾做过大量慈善来为自己塑造良好形象，从而被视为受尊重的公民，而不是靠恶习致富的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And then I asked GPT to come up with 50 people who did that and what were their vices?
turns.zh: 然后我让 GPT 列出 50 个这样做的人，以及他们的恶习是什么。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: How did they change the reputation by doing lots of philanthropy and all of that stuff?
turns.zh: 他们是如何通过大量慈善等手段改变声誉的？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Then a thing happens.
turns.zh: 然后事情就发生了（指验证的过程）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And then I research in all sorts of directions. And I have no boundaries if I go to chemistry or physics or human behavior to discover some universal principles.
turns.zh: 然后我会从各个方向去研究。无论是化学、物理还是人类行为，只要能发现某些普适原则，我都不设边界。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So my method of learning is to constantly come up with conjectures from the dots that you have connected and then absolutely work hard to find proof of it and then use that to connect to the next dot.
turns.zh: 所以我学习的方法是：不断从你已经连上的点中得出猜想，然后努力去寻找证据，再用它去连接下一个点。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I often tell people that every book you read makes your brain poorer to read the next book.
turns.zh: 所以我常跟人说，你读的每一本书，都会让你读下一本书时的大脑变得更“贫乏”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: That's the purpose of books, but that's true for every single thing we learn.
turns.zh: 这就是书的目的，但我们学到的每一件事也都是如此。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It makes our brain poorerfor the next thing that we are supposed to learn.
turns.zh: 它让我们本该去学的下一件事时，大脑变得更贫乏。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there a recent example of that where you got super sucked into some topic?
turns.zh: 有没有最近你完全沉浸进去的某个话题的例子？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Well, it's my daily life.
turns.zh: 嗯，那就是我的日常生活。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I get sucked into topics every now and then.
turns.zh: 我时不时会沉浸到某些话题里。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, I've been thinking about second order effects of AI and what happens to countries and jobs and how to expect some of these things to change, not change, rate of change, rate of skill change.
turns.zh: 比如，我一直在思考 AI 的二阶效应，以及它对国家和就业的影响，如何应对其中一些事情的变化、不变、变化速率、技能变化速率。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I got recently obsessed with what happens to lab grown diamonds if they become big?
turns.zh: 我最近痴迷于：如果实验室培育钻石变得普及，会发生什么？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Does it kill diamonds?
turns.zh: 它会毁掉天然钻石吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Does it make diamonds bigger?
turns.zh: 还是会让钻石产业变得更大？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And then I looked at parallels.
turns.zh: 然后我去寻找类比。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So, the pearl industry was very big before culture.
turns.zh: 在养殖珍珠（cultured pearls）出现之前，珍珠产业曾经非常庞大。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Cultured pearls came and the high status of pearls disappeared because everybody could have pearls.
turns.zh: 养殖珍珠出现后，珍珠的高贵地位就消失了，因为人人都能拥有珍珠。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But not too long ago, pearls were a very royal thing . Every prince and princess used to have pearls around them, but as soon as it was easy to manufacture in a lab, it lost its value.
turns.zh: 但不久前，珍珠还是非常皇室化的东西。每位王子和公主都佩戴珍珠，可一旦在实验室里就能轻易制造，它就失去了价值。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So then I think should I be shorting or going long on diamonds thinking about what happens?
turns.zh: 所以我就想，考虑到接下来会发生什么，我该做空还是做多钻石？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But there'll be a temporary period of making a lot of money on lab grown diamonds, which will kill... it'll become parasitic on the status of diamonds and destroy all of the profit pools.
turns.zh: 但会有一段时期，人们能在实验室培育钻石上赚大钱，而这会——它会寄生在钻石的地位之上，并摧毁所有的利润池。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You heard it here first, time to buy some diamond futures.
turns.zh: 你在这里先听到——是时候买点钻石期货了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I feel like there's no one in the world ChatGPT impacted more than you considering how much you want to spend digging into random topics.
turns.zh: 我觉得，考虑到你有多么想钻进各种随机话题里，世界上没人比 ChatGPT 对你的影响更大了。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I often wonder, Lenny, that if you took the most serious people and made their GPT searches public, a lot of people will learn because the problem of GPT is now it'll make the people with great questions do well, versus people who are looking for basic answers.
turns.zh: Lenny，我常想，如果你把那些最认真的人他们的 GPT 搜索公开，很多人会学到东西，因为 GPT 的问题在于，现在它会让那些提出好问题的人表现更好，而不是那些只找基础答案的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think the world is going to be unfair to people who will ask great questions.
turns.zh: 所以我认为，世界对那些会提出好问题的人将变得不公平（意指更优待）。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Interesting.
turns.zh: 有意思。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Well, I got to ask you, is there any advice you have for asking great questions that has helped you in your work and career and life?
turns.zh: 嗯，我得问你，对于提出好问题，你有什么建议吗？这曾在你的工作、事业和生活中帮助过你。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Whenever somebody has many choices and they make the right choice in whatever domain they have.
turns.zh: 每当某个人有很多选择，并在自己的领域里做出了正确的选择。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, let's say you could hire anybody but you hired great people, or let's say you could have married anybody, but you married a great person and so on and so forth. Everybody has many choices to make.
turns.zh: 比如，假设你本可以雇任何人，但你雇到了优秀的人；或者你本可以娶任何人，但你娶了一位很棒的人，诸如此类。每个人都有很多选择要做。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: How do they make choices for that domain of expertise?
turns.zh: 他们在自己擅长的领域是如何做选择的？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think that is the most, and many times they're not going to be able to explain how they make great choices.
turns.zh: 而我认为这是最（重要的）……很多时候他们甚至无法解释自己是如何做出好选择的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They'll have to really go into that because they don't really have their mental models figured out.
turns.zh: 他们得真的深入其中，因为他们其实还没把自己的心智模型想清楚。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: They cannot articulate, they cannot coach, they cannot explain.
turns.zh: 他们无法表达、无法指导、无法解释。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But if you can figure out how they make great decisions in general, in whatever domain of work they're doing, you'll find many interesting insights coming over there.
turns.zh: 但如果你能搞清楚他们一般在做决策（无论做什么工作）时是如何做出好决定的，你会发现许多有趣的洞察。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The other good question to ask is about second order thinking.
turns.zh: 另一个该问的好问题是关于二阶思维的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What do they think will happen to the world and why did they come to that conclusion?
turns.zh: 他们认为世界会发生什么，以及他们为什么会得出那个结论？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And you see that full chain of thoughts is very powerful.
turns.zh: 而你会看到，那条完整的思维链非常强大。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, second order thinking is known to be the most powerful trait to predict the success of somebody.
turns.zh: 比如，二阶思维被认为是预测一个人成功与否最有力的特征。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I often wonder what happened in the childhood of people who became great at second order thinking.
turns.zh: 但我常想，那些在二阶思维上变得很厉害的人，他们的童年发生了什么。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that question is not fully discovered or discussed yet.
turns.zh: 而那个问题还没有被充分发现或讨论。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I've found some loose examples such as if you played strategy games or only physical games as a strong correlation to building
turns.zh: 而且我发现了一些松散的例子，比如你玩策略游戏还是只玩体能游戏，与（创业）构建能力有很强的相关性。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So rigor came from physical games, but second order thinking came from playing strategy games as a kid.
turns.zh: 所以纪律来自体能游戏，但二阶思维来自小时候玩策略游戏。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you had both, you could do really well in general because you have discipline and second order thinking together.
turns.zh: 而如果你两者都有，总体就能做得很好，因为你同时具备了纪律和二阶思维。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Then did you ever have an exercise of looking at history?
turns.zh: 那么你有没有做过审视历史之类的练习？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, one of the things I recommend for parents to do with their kids, I call it the ‘Whyfi school’, is ask them one ‘why’ question every meal and let them come back with answers the next day.
turns.zh: 比如，我推荐家长和孩子做的一件事，我称之为“Whyfi 学校”，就是每顿饭问他们一个“为什么”的问题，让他们第二天带着答案回来。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, “Why do humans wear jewelry” and ”Why is something a certain way?”
turns.zh: 比如，“人类为什么要戴首饰”，以及“为什么某件事是某种样子？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And let them go into the full depth of history and find out.
turns.zh: 让他们深入到历史的最深处去探究。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Why is it so expensive to advertise in the Super Bowl?
turns.zh: 为什么在超级碗（Super Bowl）打广告那么贵？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And so on and so forth.
turns.zh: 等等。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You just take one question.
turns.zh: 你就只拿一个问题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you train them on why, they evolve at a very different rate because how, what are the questions which do not evolve at a much higher rate, because ‘why’ is the deep question and it breaks a lot of things in your head.
turns.zh: 如果你用“为什么”来训练他们，他们会以完全不同的速度进化，因为——什么样的提问不会以更高的速度进化？“为什么”是个深层问题，它会打破你脑海中的很多东西。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Or another question about origin stories that “How did elevators come into being?” and "what made your phones happen?”
turns.zh: 或者另一个关于起源故事的问题：“电梯是如何出现的？”以及“是什么让你的手机成为现实的？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: “What made microphones happen and why is it called microphone and why is it called a phone?”
turns.zh: “是什么让麦克风成为现实的？为什么它叫 microphone，为什么叫 phone？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you just want to go into this depth, you'll see people build second order thinking automatically because either you go into history and see second order thinking coming along with that, or you play games that train your brain for second order thinking with the spectrum.
turns.zh: 而如果你只想深入到这种程度，你会看到人们会自动建立起二阶思维，因为你要么深入历史、看到随之而来的二阶思维，要么玩那些训练大脑进行二阶思维的游戏。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But that's a broad range of things that I think people should be asking.
turns.zh: 但那是一大范围我认为人们应该问的事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm looking forward to Kunal’s children's raising book, like a book to help you raise kids.
turns.zh: 我期待 Kunal 的育儿书，就是一本帮你养孩子的书。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: This could be your future.
turns.zh: 这可能是你的未来。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I don't have kids so I can run experiments on everybody else's kids.
turns.zh: 我还没孩子，所以我可以在别人的孩子身上做实验。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So it's a great thing to do.
turns.zh: 所以这倒是一件好事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I feel like with these questions, I think the rule has to be you can't just ask ChatGPT for the answer if the block it-
turns.zh: 我觉得对于这些提问，规则应该是——你不能只是去问 ChatGPT 要答案，如果是那种被……的问题——

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Actually it's not bad.
turns.zh: 其实这也不坏。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think you should encourage it because we have to assume that we are going to be all co-pilots of AI now.
turns.zh: 我认为你应该鼓励它，因为我们必须假定，如今我们都将成为 AI 的副驾驶（co-pilots）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What you have to do is derive the second order insight that, “Okay, this is true.
turns.zh: 你要做的是推导出二阶洞察：“好，这是真的。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Where is the similarity of this in somewhere else?”
turns.zh: “它在别处有什么相似之处？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Give me an example of this found somewhere else, and so on and so forth.
turns.zh: “给我一个它在别处出现的例子。”等等。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Amazing.
turns.zh: 太妙了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I have just a couple more questions before we get to our very exciting lightning round.
turns.zh: 在进入到非常刺激的快问快答环节之前，我还有几个问题。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: First, let's visit the contrarian corner.
turns.zh: 首先，让我们进入“反共识角落”。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm curious. What's something that you believe that very few other people would agree with you on and why do you hold that belief?
turns.zh: 我很好奇。有什么是你相信、却很少有人会同意的观点？你又为什么持有这个信念？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Our understanding of wealth and what wealth is, is flawed.
turns.zh: 我们对财富以及财富本质的理解是有缺陷的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: To me, wealth is nothing but storage of energy.
turns.zh: 对我来说，财富不过是能量的储存。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore the reason wealth is not zero sum is because energy is, and we are just finding ways to convert energy to our advantage.
turns.zh: 所以财富不是零和游戏的原因在于能量是——我们只是在寻找把能量转化为对我们有利的方式。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We are the only species that has managed to convert all forms of energy to our advantage.
turns.zh: 我们是唯一一个成功把各种形式的能量都转化为对我们有利的物种。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Kinetic energy and fuel and sound and solar.
turns.zh: 动能、燃料、声音、太阳能。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: No other species has done this.
turns.zh: 没有其他物种做到过。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore, since the industrial revolution, our wealth has gone like this and continues to be like that.
turns.zh: 因此，自工业革命以来，我们的财富就一直这样（上升），并且持续如此。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: AI and nuclear fission and all this stuff will kind of take us right there.
turns.zh: AI、核裂变等等，会把我们带到那个高度。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I have a strong view that we will never, never have equality of wealth.
turns.zh: 所以我有很强的观点：我们永远、永远不可能实现财富均等。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: In fact, chasing that is actually a bad idea.
turns.zh: 事实上，追求那一点其实是个坏主意。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But if you let people do well and chase wealth, they have enough wealth for everybody else and we could help a lot of people out.
turns.zh: 但如果你让人们好好发展、去追逐财富，他们会有足够多的财富分给其他人，我们也可以帮助很多人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think it's complicated because we can have all these democratic arguments that wealth is concentrated and all that, but that's the physics of wealth.
turns.zh: 而且我认为这很复杂，因为我们可以有各种民主的论点说财富集中了等等，但那只是财富的“物理学”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It'll always be concentrated.
turns.zh: 它永远会是集中的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You change these mediums, companies, countries.
turns.zh: 你改变这些媒介、公司、国家。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: To me, wealth is nothing but an entropic complexity that'll keep changing its form and shape.
turns.zh: 对我来说，财富不过是一种熵式的复杂性，会不断改变它的形态和形状。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You can keep fighting it or accept its physics and reap the benefit of that physics.
turns.zh: 你可以一直对抗它，或者接受它的“物理学”并从中获益。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I think Elon had this interesting point that wealth is just a database where everyone's wealth I guess is just a row in the database and here's how much everyone has and you're just transferring numbers around and that's the whole economy.
turns.zh: 我记得埃隆有个有趣的观点：财富只是一个数据库，每个人的财富我想就是数据库里的一行，记录着每个人有多少，你只是在四处转移数字，这就是整个经济。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: No, but the nuance that is important is that you can actually increase the database size infinitely.
turns.zh: 不，但重要的细微差别是，你其实可以无限地扩大这个数据库的规模。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That's true.
turns.zh: 没错。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore his vision of the sun's energy, if you really convert all the energy to our advantage, the amount of wealth we will create for humans is disproportionate.
turns.zh: 因此，按照他关于太阳能量的愿景，如果你真的把所有能量都转化为对我们有利，我们为人类创造的财富将是 disproportionally（不成比例地巨大）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And all the species that are managed to collaborate and cooperate to create wealth, for example, let's define wealth as biomass.
turns.zh: 而所有那些成功协作、合作来创造财富的物种——比如，我们把财富定义为生物量（biomass）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So let's say ants and bacteria and humans are the only few things that have the largest biomass on this planet because we figured out how to make energy work to our advantage.
turns.zh: 那么比如蚂蚁、细菌和人类，是地球上仅有的拥有最大生物量的少数物种，因为我们弄明白了如何让能量为我们所用。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I love all the directions we've gone.
turns.zh: 我喜欢我们走过的所有这些方向。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Probably the last question, is there a story of failure in your career that would be interesting to share?
turns.zh: 可能是最后一个问题了，你职业生涯中有没有一段有趣的失败故事可以分享？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Something that taught you an important lesson?
turns.zh: 某个教会了你重要教训的事？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's a series of failures.
turns.zh: 是一系列失败。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think there is no escape for anybody who's done anything in life, not failed a lot, like every day, every thing.
turns.zh: 我认为，任何在生活中做成过事的人，都逃不开大量失败，几乎每天、每件事都在失败。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I would say that many initiatives, many products, companies that I've built have absolutely failed, hirings that have failed, trust broken, betrayals.
turns.zh: 但我想说，我发起的许多举措、打造的许多产品、创办的许多公司都彻底失败了，招聘失败过、信任破裂过、遭遇过背叛。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think there is no end to it.
turns.zh: 所以我认为这没有尽头。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I think entrepreneurs have this weird ability to forget about failures and almost turn that into a lesson that you hold, and you forget the story.
turns.zh: 但我认为创业者有一种奇怪的能力——忘记失败，几乎把失败变成你牢记的教训，而忘记具体的故事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, COVID has literally no memory for me.
turns.zh: 比如，新冠对我来说几乎毫无记忆。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I just don't remember what was COVID.
turns.zh: 我就是不记得新冠时是什么样。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's just a blank in my head right now.
turns.zh: 现在我脑海里就是一片空白。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think that humans are great at forgetting the memory of failure, but remember the lesson from failure.
turns.zh: 而我认为，人类很擅长忘记失败的记忆，却记住失败的教训。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I think I'm constantly learning, and I often believe that life is too short to make all our mistakes ourselves.
turns.zh: 但我认为我一直在学习，而且我常相信，生命太短，不能只靠自己犯下所有的错误。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So we should be learning from other people's failures as well.
turns.zh: 所以我们也应该从别人的失败中学习。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And a lot of times we don't do that because we believe that we are special, nothing like that will happen to us, but as humans, we should be learning.
turns.zh: 很多时候我们不这么做，是因为我们认为自己特殊，那种事不会发生在我们身上，但作为人，我们应该学习。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I would say that my life started from a failure.
turns.zh: 我想说，我的人生始于一次失败。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: My family went through a severe financial crisis.
turns.zh: 我的家庭经历过一场严重的财务危机。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I had to start working from age 15 and I feel till date, I'm just trying to escape that failure that happened in the family.
turns.zh: 我从 15 岁就开始工作，而且直到今天，我都只是在试图逃离那次发生在家里的失败。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I think many of us are just fighting that initial large failure that we've had and don't want to be anywhere near that.
turns.zh: 所以我认为我们很多人只是在对抗最初那次巨大的失败，不愿再靠近它一步。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And although we are significantly far away from that, the feeling is exactly that.
turns.zh: 而且尽管我们已经远远脱离了那个处境，但那种感觉依然如故。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Circles back to one of our first few questions about the chips on shoulders driving a lot of motivation.
turns.zh: 这又回到了我们最早几个问题之一：肩上的刺（证明自己的执念）驱动了大量的动力。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's this phrase, ”Chips on shoulders drive chips in pockets.”
turns.zh: 有句话是：“肩上的刺，换来口袋里的筹码（芯片）。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: That's interesting.
turns.zh: 这很有意思。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there anything more you want to share about that early challenge you ran into or is that something you've shared often?
turns.zh: 关于你早年遇到的那个挑战，还有什么想分享的吗？还是说这你已经常分享过了？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: No, I mean I've shared that enough, but I used to not talk about it before because I used to think that I would get some sympathy for that.
turns.zh: 不，我的意思是已经分享得够多了，但我以前不怎么提，因为我曾以为那样会得到一些同情。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And only in the recent past did I speak about it because I want people to realize that I was not some gifted kid who had some rich parents who made me extraordinarily bright and put me in great schools and colleges and I made my way through that.
turns.zh: 直到最近我才谈起，因为我想让人们意识到，我并不是什么天生聪颖、有有钱父母把我送进好学校好大学、然后我顺着这条路走出来的孩子。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I used to not talk about it earlier because there's a lot of tendency to give sympathy to those people who say, "Oh, this guy had struggled."
turns.zh: 我以前不提，是因为人们往往很容易同情那些说“噢，这家伙曾经挣扎过”的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I don't want to be given any credit for playing that poverty card or this card or struggling for food card.
turns.zh: 而我不想因为打“贫困牌”“这个牌”或“为食物挣扎牌”而获得任何认可。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: That's not an excuse.
turns.zh: 那不是借口。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: There are so many people in the world who've done extraordinarily well because they had the gift of struggle.
turns.zh: 世界上有太多人之所以做得极其出色，正是因为他们拥有“挣扎”这份礼物。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I often tell people that this is the biggest curse of successful parents, that that's the only gift they'll not be able to give to their kids, the gift of struggle that they had.
turns.zh: 而且我常跟人说，这是成功父母最大的诅咒——他们唯一无法给孩子的礼物，正是他们自己曾有过的“挣扎”这份礼物。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I think about that a lot.
turns.zh: 我经常思考这一点。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We have a kid, he's eight months now, and so I'm trying to figure out the balance of struggle versus making life easy and great, a new challenge for me to figure out.
turns.zh: 我们有个孩子，现在八个月大，所以我在努力寻找“挣扎”与“让生活轻松美好”之间的平衡，这对我来说是个新挑战。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Before we get to a very exciting lightning round, is there anything else, Kunal, you wanted to share or leave listeners with?
turns.zh: 在进入非常刺激的快问快答之前，Kunal，还有什么你想分享的、或想留给听众的话吗？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Anything?
turns.zh: 任何？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Any last nuggets of thoughts?
turns.zh: 最后还有什么思想金句吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Well, I would love for the listeners from different fields of product to share what you're learning without being fearful of the judgment of your peers, because there are many, many people who are learning only because you share your evolution and your thoughts.
turns.zh: 嗯，我希望来自不同产品领域的听众，能毫无畏惧于同行评判地分享你们正在学到的东西，因为有太多人之所以在学习，正是因为你们分享了自己的成长和想法。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I believe that a lot more could be contributing.
turns.zh: 而且我相信，能有更多人做出贡献。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And a lot of your listeners are really bright people.
turns.zh: 你的很多听众都是非常聪明的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: If they all shared, many people from many places in the world would learn and achieve some amount of success.
turns.zh: 如果他们都能分享，世界上很多地方的人都会学到东西，并取得一定程度的成功。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Thanks to your sharing.
turns.zh: 多亏了你的分享。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Amazing.
turns.zh: 太棒了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: With that, we've reached our very exciting lightning round.
turns.zh: 话不多说，我们进入了非常刺激的快问快答环节。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Are you ready?
turns.zh: 准备好了吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: All set.
turns.zh: 完全准备好了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Let's do it.
turns.zh: 开始吧。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: First question, what are two or three books that you've recommended most to other people?
turns.zh: 第一个问题，你最常推荐给别人的两三本书是什么？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It keeps changing a lot, but my books are usually around understanding human behavior.
turns.zh: 这个一直在变，但我推荐的书通常都是关于理解人类行为的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I keep changing based on the person, but I think it's the biggest subject.
turns.zh: 我会根据人不同而换，但我认为这是最大的主题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: All our customers, all our investors, all our employees, all our relationships are all humans.
turns.zh: 我们所有的客户、所有的投资者、所有的员工、所有的关系，都是人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the subject that we are weakest on is human behavior.
turns.zh: 而我们所最薄弱的学科，就是人类行为。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And how do we live this life?
turns.zh: 以及我们该如何过这一生？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We are playing life on extremely hard mode if you don't learn human behavior.
turns.zh: 如果你不学习人类行为，你就是在以极高难度模式玩人生。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I would say that's one thing.
turns.zh: 所以我想说，这是其一。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The second thing, evolutionary biology, teaches a lot about how species evolve and how they make decisions and what are the core motivations that drive everybody.
turns.zh: 第二，进化生物学，能教给我们很多关于物种如何进化、如何做决策，以及驱动每个人的核心动机是什么。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So that's another one I would recommend.
turns.zh: 所以那是我会推荐的另一类。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I don't want to make a recommendation because I can barely finish a book to be honest.
turns.zh: 而且我不想给出具体推荐，因为说实话，我几乎读不完一本书。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So I believe in drifting and getting deeper into topics.
turns.zh: 所以我更相信“漂流”式地深入各种话题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So understanding the topics versus trying to say, give me these three books and I'm going to be good.
turns.zh: 所以是理解话题本身，而不是说“给我这三本书，我就好了”。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And the last one I would say, is that anything that can make you learn something about their journey versus their success.
turns.zh: 而我会说的最后一类，是任何能让你学到关于他们“历程”而非“成功”的东西。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So sometimes autobiographies are too celebratory in some ways, but if you can just kind of understand how… any book that can teach you about how people recover from a setback in great detail is a great book to learn from.
turns.zh: 所以有时自传在某些方面过于歌功颂德，但如果你能理解……任何能详尽教你人们如何从挫折中恢复的书的，都是值得学习的好书。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: An audience member on Twitter actually asked a similar question along these lines, if there's one book that you could read over and over and over, what would that be?
turns.zh: Twitter 上一位观众其实问过类似的问题：如果有一本书你可以一读再读，那会是什么？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Is there one?
turns.zh: 有吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I absolutely don't believe in reading over and over because I believe that we are evolving.
turns.zh: 我绝对不相信反复读同一本书，因为我相信我们是在不断进化的。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: You might discover the same stuff coming from different books and you would say, "Oh, I can categorize this in my brain again and again."
turns.zh: 你可能会从不同书中发现同样的东西，然后说“噢，我可以一遍遍在脑子里把它归类。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But I think we tend to become believers, and it becomes too religious if you repeat.
turns.zh: 但我认为，如果反复重复，我们会变成信徒，变得太“宗教化”了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yeah.
turns.zh: 嗯。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Next question, do you have a favorite recent movie or TV show that you've really enjoyed?
turns.zh: 下一个问题，你最近有没有特别喜欢的电影或剧集？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I love Oppenheimer because of the struggles and Nolan's craft of making the movies, but nothing in the recent past that I feel is right up there.
turns.zh: 我喜欢《奥本海默》，因为其中的挣扎和诺兰拍电影的手艺，但近期没有哪部让我觉得能与之比肩。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite interview question that you like to ask candidates that you're interviewing?
turns.zh: 你有没有喜欢问面试候选人的招牌问题？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I like to ask a hypothetical second order thinking question.
turns.zh: 我喜欢问一个假设性的二阶思维问题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, if everybody who has taken a COVID vaccine dies tonight, what happens in 12 months from now?
turns.zh: 比如：如果今晚所有接种过新冠疫苗的人全都死掉了，12 个月后会发生什么？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Can you explain the world- from what happens to money, what happens to law?
turns.zh: 你能解释这个世界吗——钱会怎样、法律会怎样？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What happens to countries?
turns.zh: 国家会怎样？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What happens to the military?
turns.zh: 军队会怎样？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What happens to the stock market?
turns.zh: 股市会怎样？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What happens to the order of things?
turns.zh: 事物的秩序会怎样？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I would say less than 10% of really smart people can have really good answers.
turns.zh: 而我想说，不到 10% 真正聪明的人能给出真正好的答案。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So it tells you how good they are at second order thinking.
turns.zh: 所以这能告诉你他们的二阶思维有多强。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But the questions can keep changing.
turns.zh: 但问题可以不断变化。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, if you said that, what if arranged marriages were banned in India, and you got capital punishment for doing arranged marriages?
turns.zh: 比如，假设你说：如果印度禁止包办婚姻，而且包办婚姻会被判死刑？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: What happens to the country?
turns.zh: 国家会怎样？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: How do we change from there?
turns.zh: 我们会从那里如何改变？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Like some absurd scenarios, but then what happens after that?
turns.zh: 就像一些荒诞的场景，但之后又会发生什么？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Not to give away your secret sauce, but what do you look for in an answer that gives you a sense there?
turns.zh: 不是要泄露你的秘方，但你在答案里寻找什么线索，能让你感觉到（这个人行不行）？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The range of things that they could go into and think about- if this happens, B happens and then C happens.
turns.zh: 他们能深入并思考的事情的范围——如果 A 发生，B 就发生，然后 C 发生。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The leaps they could make.
turns.zh: 以及他们能做出的思维跳跃。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And just so people understand, when you're talking about second order thinking, what's the simplest way to describe that concept?
turns.zh: 为了让大家理解，当你谈二阶思维时，最简单的描述方式是什么？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I think the simplest way to think about this is being able to correctly judge the butterfly effect of an event as close as possible.
turns.zh: 我认为最简单的理解方式是：能够尽可能准确地判断一个事件的蝴蝶效应。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: For example, a lot of people in the stock market use that to say how stocks will go up and down.
turns.zh: 比如，很多股市里的人用它来预测股票会如何涨跌。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: There's something that has happened in the market.
turns.zh: 市场里发生了某件事。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: “Oh, there is a war now with Russia, then what happens to the market?”
turns.zh: “噢，现在和俄罗斯开战了，那市场会怎样？”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Can you be good at predicting that?
turns.zh: 你能很好地预测吗？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: But in everything in life, if this happens, a lot of people hate this because it's very taxing to the brain.
turns.zh: 但在生活的每件事里，如果这件事发生……很多人讨厌这个，因为它非常耗费脑力。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The brain absolutely hates second order thinking unless you've trained your brain with second order thinking all the time that it looks forward to it.
turns.zh: 大脑绝对讨厌二阶思维，除非你一直用二阶思维训练大脑，让它开始期待这种思考。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So you convert this into a hate versus a reward cycle, and that comes with probably doing it early on in your life.
turns.zh: 所以你要把它从“厌恶循环”转化为“奖励循环”，而这大概需要你在早年就开始做。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: Later on, people hate doing second order thinking.
turns.zh: 之后，人们就讨厌做二阶思维了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It is.
turns.zh: 确实。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Yes.
turns.zh: 是的。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That sounds like a lot of work for the brain.
turns.zh: 那听起来对大脑来说是很费劲的工作。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Okay.
turns.zh: 好。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just a few more questions.
turns.zh: 就剩几个问题了。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite product that you've recently discovered and that you really love?
turns.zh: 你最近有没有发现什么特别喜欢的产品？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I'm looking forward to my Vision Pro coming soon.
turns.zh: 我正期待着我的 Vision Pro 尽快到货。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: It's a future favorite product.
turns.zh: 它是我未来的最爱产品。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: We have actually Boz from Meta coming on as the next guest in my recording.
turns.zh: 其实 Meta 的 Boz 会作为我下一位录制嘉宾出场。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm not sure when they come out in sequence, but we're going to talk about his thoughts.
turns.zh: 我不确定播出顺序，但我们会聊聊他的想法。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: The most fascinating thing that I saw was Zuck talking about the utility of Meta being better than Vision Pro and their product.
turns.zh: 我看到最有趣的事是小扎在说 Meta 的实用性比 Vision Pro 和他们的产品更好。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And that's exactly going to work well for Apple because when you try to make the product more utilitarian, it loses status.
turns.zh: 而这恰恰会对苹果有利，因为当你试图让产品更实用时，它就失去了地位（光环）。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And if you study animals, you realize that the one which gets the highest mating success is the one which can demonstrate the ability to waste resources and not be very efficient with resources.
turns.zh: 而如果你研究动物，你会发现，交配成功率最高的，是那些能展示自己“浪费资源、不善于高效利用资源”能力的个体。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And therefore people who are known to buy a product that is wasteful will actually own higher status.
turns.zh: 所以，那些以购买“浪费型”产品而闻名的人，实际上拥有更高的地位。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think Zuck made it actually quite easy for Apple to demonstrate their superior positioning by saying that, "Oh, we are not as efficient, we are not as cheap.
turns.zh: 而我认为，小扎通过说“噢，我们没那么高效、没那么便宜”，其实让苹果很容易地展示了自己的优越定位。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: We are not for everybody."
turns.zh: “我们不是为所有人准备的。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Wow.
turns.zh: 哇。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Just continue to blow minds even on our lightning round.
turns.zh: 即使在快问快答环节，你也能继续让人大开眼界。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Do you have a favorite life motto that you often come back to share with friends and family, find useful in work or in life?
turns.zh: 你有没有一句最喜欢的人生格言，会经常拿来分享给朋友和家人，或是在工作生活中觉得有用？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: It's not a favorite motto, but I think we truly are transient and we are very lucky to have this life that we have and we have to make the most out of it.
turns.zh: 它不是什么最喜欢的格言，但我认为我们真的是转瞬即逝的，能拥有这样的人生非常幸运，我们必须充分利用它。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And all these struggles will mean nothing.
turns.zh: 而这一切挣扎终将毫无意义。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I often tell people that you should wish for your life to be so great that you have collected the highest amount of content when you are old, and you have no end to the stories that you can talk about.
turns.zh: 我常跟人说，你应该希望自己的人生足够精彩，以至于年老时你收集了最多的“素材”，而且有讲不完的故事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: That reminds me of a book I once read that really had an impact on me where somebody was trying to make a movie of their life and the producer was like, "There's nothing.
turns.zh: 这让我想起我曾读过一本对我影响很大的书：有人想把自己的人生拍成电影，制片人说：“什么都没有。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: There's no good movie here.
turns.zh: “这里没有好电影。”

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: You have not done enough interesting things."
turns.zh: “你做的事还不够有趣。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I love it.
turns.zh: 我喜欢。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so he turned his lens of what to do in life, by thinking what would make a great story.
turns.zh: 于是他转变了看待“人生该做什么”的视角，开始想什么能构成一个好故事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so he just started to do a a great story, something where you overcome challenges and achieve something you wanted.
turns.zh: 于是他就开始去书写一个好故事——一个你克服挑战、实现心愿的故事。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And so that became his life motto.
turns.zh: 于是那成了他的人生格言。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: “I'm going to try hard things and overcome them.
turns.zh: “我要去尝试艰难的事并克服它们。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: And that's going to be my life.”
turns.zh: “那才是我的人生。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I love it.
turns.zh: 我喜欢。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I love it.
turns.zh: 我喜欢。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I love it.
turns.zh: 我喜欢。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'll link to that book in the show notes.
turns.zh: 我会在节目笔记里放上那本书的链接。

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: Final question, do you have this series on Twitter that you call Monday Motivations?
turns.zh: 最后一个问题，你在 Twitter 上是不是有一个叫“周一动力”（Monday Motivations）的系列？

turns.speaker: Lenny
turns.en: I'm curious what's motivating you these days?
turns.zh: 我很好奇，这些天是什么在激励着你？

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I find the internet is filled with all these people trying to give fake motivation and make money off that stuff.
turns.zh: 我发现互联网上充斥着各种试图提供虚假动力、并靠这个赚钱的人。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And it's almost like a drug for people to feel, ”Oh my God, there's motivation, I'm going to do well.”
turns.zh: 这几乎成了人们的一种毒品——让人感觉“天哪，有动力了，我要变好了。”

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: I just wanted to remind people that all success comes from an extraordinary amount of pain and struggle and hard work, and there is no shortcut to anything material coming in life.
turns.zh: 我只是想提醒人们：所有的成功都来自极其巨大的痛苦、挣扎和努力，而人生中任何物质上的收获都没有捷径。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And so the Monday motivation post comes as the anti-motivation post because the world is filled with... I believe that the biggest profit making scheme that I've seen in recent times is to tell people to love themselves and they'll pay you money for saying that.
turns.zh: 所以“周一动力”这个帖子其实是以“反动力”的形式出现的，因为这个世界充满了……我认为近年来我见过最大的赚钱套路，就是告诉人们要爱自己，然后他们会为这句话付钱给你。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think the best way to love yourself is to keep evolving.
turns.zh: 而我认为爱自己最好的方式，就是不断进化。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: So my motivation comes from evolution, connecting dots, solving harder problems than I've solved in the past.
turns.zh: 所以我的动力来自进化、连接点、解决比我过去解决过的更难的问题。

turns.speaker: KUNAL SHAH
turns.en: And I think life is ultimately a game where you want to feel that your levels have changed and your skills have changed constantly.
turns.zh: 而且我认为，人生归根结底是一场游戏，你想要感受到自己的等级变了、技能也一直在变。
